## The number most guides give you is the best case

Search for Uttarakhand PCS salary and you will find a figure, usually somewhere between Rs 80,000 and Rs 95,000 a month, presented as what a newly appointed officer earns.

That figure is not wrong. It is the top of a range, and it assumes a posting in Dehradun.

Uttarakhand is a hill state. Most of its districts are not Dehradun, and the allowance that varies most with posting is house rent allowance, which runs at 27 per cent of basic pay in a city classified X, 18 per cent in a Y-class city, and 9 per cent in a Z-class or rural location. On a basic pay of Rs 56,100, that difference is worth over Rs 10,000 a month between the best and worst case, before anything else is counted.

Working against that, Uttarakhand postings can attract hill and difficult-area allowances that a plains state does not offer, which pushes in the opposite direction.

So the honest answer to what Uttarakhand PCS pays is: it depends substantially on where you are posted, and the arithmetic below sets out what that means in rupees.

## Start with the basic pay

The Deputy Collector and Sub Divisional Magistrate post, along with Deputy Superintendent of Police, sits at Pay Level 10 of the 7th Pay Commission matrix, with an entry basic pay of Rs 56,100 a month.

That single figure is the foundation for everything else, because most allowances are calculated as a percentage of basic pay rather than as flat amounts. A change in basic pay therefore moves the whole package.

One clarification that matters and is routinely glossed over: the UKPSC Combined Upper Subordinate Services examination recruits to a range of posts, and they do not all sit at Level 10. Deputy Collector and DSP are the senior posts in the combined service. Other posts recruited through the same examination, including some revenue and development positions, sit at lower pay levels with correspondingly lower basic pay.

So a single figure for "Uttarakhand PCS salary" is misleading unless the post is specified. The notification for each cycle states the pay scale for each post, and that is the document to check rather than a general article. What follows uses the Level 10 Deputy Collector and DSP position, since that is what most candidates mean.

## Dearness allowance

Dearness allowance is paid as a percentage of basic pay and revised periodically to track inflation.

The rate applicable following the July 2025 revision was 50 per cent of basic pay. Reporting suggests an increase to 53 per cent from January 2026, though a future revision is an expectation rather than a settled figure until it is notified, so treat it accordingly.

At 50 per cent on a basic of Rs 56,100, dearness allowance is Rs 28,050 a month. At 53 per cent it would be Rs 29,733.

Two things follow. Dearness allowance is the largest single addition to basic pay at this level, larger than house rent allowance even in a Dehradun posting. And because it is revised twice a year, the same post pays measurably more in December than it did in January of the same year, which is why salary figures quoted in older articles understate current pay.

## House rent allowance, and why your posting decides it

This is where the range in Uttarakhand comes from.

| City classification | HRA rate | On Rs 56,100 basic |
|---|---|---|
| X class, Dehradun | 27 per cent | Rs 15,147 |
| Y class | 18 per cent | Rs 10,098 |
| Z class and rural | 9 per cent | Rs 5,049 |

The spread between a Dehradun posting and a rural one is roughly Rs 10,100 a month, which is around Rs 1.2 lakh a year on house rent allowance alone.

The important qualification is that house rent allowance is generally payable where government accommodation is not provided. An officer allotted official accommodation, which is common for a Sub Divisional Magistrate at a sub-division headquarters, typically does not draw HRA. That is not a loss: free or heavily subsidised housing at a location where private rent is low is usually worth more than 9 per cent of basic in cash.

Which is the first honest point about a hill-state posting. A rural posting shows a lower cash salary and often a lower cost of living, with accommodation provided. Comparing the cash figure alone across postings tells you very little about what you actually have left at the end of the month.

## Hill and difficult area allowances

This is the Uttarakhand-specific element that generic PCS salary articles omit entirely, because they are written from the central pay rules without reference to the state's geography.

Postings in hill areas and difficult or remote locations attract additional allowances under the applicable rules, intended to compensate for altitude, isolation, harder living conditions and the cost of goods that must be transported up.

The rates and the classification of specific locations are set by the state government and revised from time to time, so a candidate should establish the current position from the state's own orders rather than from a secondary source. What is worth knowing structurally is that the allowance exists, that it applies precisely to the postings where house rent allowance is lowest, and that it therefore partially offsets the geographic variation described above.

The practical consequence is that the total package in a remote hill posting is closer to a Dehradun posting than the house rent allowance difference alone suggests. It is not equal, but the gap narrows.

## Putting it together: three worked examples

Using entry basic pay of Rs 56,100 and dearness allowance at 50 per cent, here is roughly how the arithmetic falls for three posting types. These are illustrative rather than payslips, since transport allowance, hill allowance rates and deductions vary.

**Dehradun posting, no government accommodation.** Basic Rs 56,100 plus dearness allowance Rs 28,050 plus house rent allowance at 27 per cent, Rs 15,147, plus transport allowance, gives gross pay in the region of Rs 1,00,000 or slightly above before deductions.

**District headquarters, Y class, no government accommodation.** Basic Rs 56,100 plus dearness allowance Rs 28,050 plus house rent allowance at 18 per cent, Rs 10,098, plus transport allowance, gives gross pay in the region of Rs 95,000 before deductions.

**Remote hill sub-division, government accommodation provided.** Basic Rs 56,100 plus dearness allowance Rs 28,050, no house rent allowance because accommodation is provided, plus hill and difficult area allowance at the applicable rate, plus transport allowance. Cash gross is lower, in the region of Rs 90,000 depending on the hill allowance rate, but housing costs nothing and local living costs are lower.

From gross, deductions apply: the National Pension System contribution at 10 per cent of basic plus dearness allowance, which on these figures is around Rs 8,400 a month, along with health scheme contributions, professional tax and income tax.

So the widely quoted range of Rs 80,000 to Rs 95,000 in hand is reasonable as a description of the middle of the distribution, with a Dehradun posting at the top and a remote posting with accommodation lower in cash but not necessarily worse in real terms.

## What the job pays beyond the payslip

At this level the non-cash component is substantial and frequently ignored in salary comparisons.

Official accommodation, where provided, removes the largest single household expense. Official transport at the appropriate level removes another. Medical facilities cover the officer and dependants. There is a defined leave entitlement, leave travel concession, and pension provision under the applicable rules, which for current recruits means the National Pension System.

Then there is the part that does not appear in any table: a Sub Divisional Magistrate holds statutory magisterial and revenue powers over a defined territory within a year or two of joining. A Deputy Superintendent of Police commands a sub-division of the police force. The responsibility and the discretion attached to these posts at that career stage are not available in private employment at comparable pay, and for most people who take these examinations that is the actual attraction rather than the salary.

## How pay grows over a career

| Stage | Pay level | Approximate basic at entry to the stage |
|---|---|---|
| Deputy Collector, SDM, DSP | Level 10 | Rs 56,100 |
| Senior scale, Additional District Magistrate level | Level 11 to 12 | Rises with each level |
| Selection grade and above | Level 13 onward | Rises with each level |

Progression within the state service runs on seniority, performance and available vacancies in the higher grades, and pay rises both through annual increments within a level and through movement to a higher level.

Separately, officers of the state civil service are eligible in due course for promotion to the Indian Administrative Service through the promotion quota, subject to the applicable rules, service length and selection process. That is a slower route than direct IAS entry and it is not available to everyone, but it exists and it materially changes the ceiling for those who reach it.

The practical implication for a candidate weighing this against private sector pay is that the comparison should be made across a career rather than at entry. Private pay at graduate entry can exceed Rs 56,100 plus allowances; the trajectory, security and non-cash components over twenty-five years are a different calculation entirely.

## How Uttarakhand compares with other state services

The 7th Pay Commission matrix applies across central and most state services, so the basic pay for an equivalent post is broadly similar between states. What differs is the allowance structure.

House rent allowance depends on how the state's cities are classified, and a state with a metropolitan X-class city offers a higher rate to officers posted there than a state without one.

Hill, tribal and difficult-area allowances exist in states with the relevant geography, so Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and the North Eastern states offer allowances that a plains state does not.

Cost of living varies enormously and moves in the opposite direction to the allowance in many cases. Dehradun is cheaper than a metropolitan capital while offering the top house rent allowance rate, which is a favourable combination.

State-specific allowances and facilities differ, and states occasionally revise their own components independently of central revisions.

For a candidate choosing which state examinations to sit, the honest guidance is that pay differences between states at this level are modest compared with the difference between clearing a state examination and not clearing one. Sit the examinations you are eligible for, including your home state and others, rather than optimising for an allowance structure.

## Transport allowance and the smaller components

The components below house rent allowance are smaller but they are not trivial across a year.

Transport allowance is paid at a rate depending on the pay level and the classification of the city of posting, with dearness allowance applied on top of it. At Level 10 in a higher-classified city it runs to a few thousand rupees a month, and in a lower-classified location somewhat less.

An important interaction: officers provided with official transport generally do not draw transport allowance, in the same way that officers in government accommodation do not draw house rent allowance. At Sub Divisional Magistrate and Deputy Superintendent of Police level, official transport is commonly available for duty, which again reduces the cash figure while removing an expense.

Beyond that, the package includes leave travel concession on the applicable cycle, medical facilities for the officer and dependants, and the leave entitlement of a state government officer. Newly appointed officers also draw pay during the probationary and training period, and the terms of that period are set out in the service rules.

The general pattern is worth internalising. At this level a substantial part of the remuneration arrives as facilities rather than as money, and the officers with the lowest cash salary are often the ones receiving the most in facilities because they are posted where facilities are provided and cash allowances are low.

## Reading a salary claim critically

Since this page exists partly to correct an over-simplified figure, it is worth setting out how to judge the next salary article you read on any government post.

Check whether the figure is gross or in-hand. A gross figure before the National Pension System contribution, health scheme, professional tax and income tax can be Rs 15,000 or more above what actually reaches the account.

Check which posting it assumes. Any figure quoting the top house rent allowance rate is describing the best case, and in a hill state that is a minority of postings.

Check the dearness allowance rate used. An article written a year ago using a lower rate understates current pay, and one projecting a future revision overstates it until that revision is notified.

Check whether accommodation and transport are assumed as cash or as facilities, because the two produce very different numbers for the same officer.

Check whether the post is specified. In a combined service recruiting across pay levels, a single figure attributed to the whole examination is not meaningful.

Apply those five checks and most published salary figures resolve into a range rather than a number, which is what they always were.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is the basic pay for Uttarakhand PCS?**
The Deputy Collector and Sub Divisional Magistrate post, along with Deputy Superintendent of Police, sits at Pay Level 10 of the 7th Pay Commission matrix with an entry basic pay of Rs 56,100 a month. Note that the UKPSC Combined Upper Subordinate Services examination also recruits to posts at lower pay levels, so the pay scale for the specific post is what the notification states.

**What is the in-hand salary of an Uttarakhand PCS officer?**
Commonly quoted at Rs 80,000 to Rs 95,000 a month for a newly appointed officer, which is reasonable as a description of the middle of the range. A Dehradun posting without government accommodation sits at the top, in the region of Rs 1,00,000 gross, while a remote posting with accommodation provided shows lower cash pay but no housing cost. Deductions for the National Pension System, health scheme, professional tax and income tax apply to all of these.

**How much is dearness allowance for Uttarakhand PCS?**
Dearness allowance was 50 per cent of basic pay following the July 2025 revision, which is Rs 28,050 on a basic of Rs 56,100. Reporting suggests an increase to 53 per cent from January 2026, which would make it Rs 29,733, though a future revision is an expectation rather than a settled figure until notified. Dearness allowance is the largest single addition to basic pay at this level.

**Why does Uttarakhand PCS salary vary so much by posting?**
Because house rent allowance is set by city classification: 27 per cent of basic in X-class Dehradun, 18 per cent in a Y-class city and 9 per cent in a Z-class or rural location. On Rs 56,100 basic that is a spread of roughly Rs 10,100 a month, or about Rs 1.2 lakh a year. Uttarakhand is a hill state where most districts are not Dehradun, so the geographic variation is larger in practice than in a state with several large cities.

**Do Uttarakhand PCS officers get a hill allowance?**
Postings in hill areas and difficult or remote locations attract additional allowances under the applicable state rules, intended to compensate for altitude, isolation and higher costs of transported goods. Rates and the classification of specific locations are set by the state government and revised periodically, so establish the current position from the state's own orders. Structurally, this allowance applies precisely where house rent allowance is lowest, so it partially offsets the geographic variation.

**Is a rural posting worse paid than a Dehradun posting?**
In cash terms yes, mainly through the lower house rent allowance, but the comparison is misleading on its own. Government accommodation is commonly provided at sub-division headquarters, which removes the largest household expense, local living costs are lower, and hill or difficult-area allowances apply where house rent allowance does not. Comparing cash salary across postings tells you little about what remains at the end of the month.

**What deductions apply to an Uttarakhand PCS salary?**
The National Pension System contribution at 10 per cent of basic plus dearness allowance, which on entry figures is around Rs 8,400 a month, along with health scheme contributions, professional tax and income tax. Current recruits come under the National Pension System rather than the older defined-benefit pension, which is a material difference from what long-serving officers receive.

**How does Uttarakhand PCS pay grow over a career?**
Through annual increments within a pay level and through movement to higher levels: Level 10 at entry, then senior scale and Additional District Magistrate level around Levels 11 and 12, then selection grade and above from Level 13. Progression depends on seniority, performance and vacancies in higher grades. Separately, state civil service officers are eligible in due course for promotion to the Indian Administrative Service through the promotion quota, subject to the applicable rules and selection.

**Which posts does the UKPSC Combined Upper Subordinate examination recruit to?**
A range of posts across the state administration, with Deputy Collector or Sub Divisional Magistrate and Deputy Superintendent of Police as the senior positions at Pay Level 10, alongside other revenue and development posts at lower pay levels. Because the levels differ, a single figure for Uttarakhand PCS salary is misleading unless the post is specified, and the notification for each cycle states the scale for each post.

**Is Uttarakhand PCS pay better than other state services?**
Broadly similar at the same level, since the 7th Pay Commission matrix applies across most state services, so basic pay for an equivalent post does not differ much. What varies is the allowance structure: city classification determines house rent allowance rates, and hill, tribal and difficult-area allowances exist only in states with the relevant geography. Dehradun offers the top house rent allowance rate at a lower cost of living than a metropolitan capital, which is a favourable combination.

**Should I choose a state examination based on salary?**
No. Pay differences between states at this level are modest compared with the difference between clearing a state examination and not clearing one. Sit every examination you are eligible for, including your home state and others, rather than optimising for an allowance structure you cannot control and which is revised periodically anyway.

**How does this compare with a private sector salary?**
Private pay at graduate entry can exceed Rs 56,100 plus allowances, so at the point of joining the comparison is not automatically favourable. The difference lies in trajectory, security, the non-cash components including accommodation, transport, medical cover and pension provision, and the statutory authority attached to these posts within a year or two of joining. That last element has no private equivalent at comparable pay, and for most candidates it is the actual reason for sitting the examination.

title: LIC AAO 2026: The Highest-Paying Exam Nobody Talks About
description: LIC AAO pays about Rs 1,26,000 a month at entry, more than an IAS officer starts on. Check the pattern, why there is no negative marking and how to prepare.
author: Mahitosh Dey
content:
## The pay figure most candidates never check

An LIC Assistant Administrative Officer starts on a basic pay of Rs 88,635, in a scale running to Rs 1,69,025. With house rent allowance, city compensatory allowance, travel and petrol allowances, the package in an A-class city works out to approximately Rs 1,26,000 a month.

Now hold that against the posts that dominate every discussion of government careers. An IAS officer entering through UPSC Civil Services starts at Pay Level 10 with a basic of Rs 56,100 and an in-hand figure around Rs 1,00,000 in a metro. A state PCS officer at the same level takes home Rs 80,000 to Rs 95,000.

LIC AAO pays more at entry than either.

That is not a typo or a marketing claim. It is a consequence of LIC operating its own pay structure as a public sector insurer, revised through its own settlements rather than through the central Pay Commission matrix, and it is why an examination that receives a fraction of the attention given to UPSC or banking recruitment quietly offers one of the strongest entry packages available to a graduate.

The notification for 2026 is expected in August 2026 on licindia.in and had not been released at the time of writing, so this is a live opportunity rather than a retrospective.

## Where the cycle stands

| Item | Position |
|---|---|
| Notification | Expected August 2026, not yet released |
| Portal | licindia.in |
| Application fee | Rs 700 general, Rs 85 for SC, ST and PwBD |

Because the notification is not out, vacancy counts and exact dates are not established. Any specific figure circulating now is a projection. Watch licindia.in rather than aggregator sites, since LIC publishes there and the recruitment details are fixed in that document.

The practical implication of an August notification is that the preparation window is now. These recruitments typically move from notification to preliminary examination within a couple of months, which is not enough time to build a base from scratch.

## The selection process, and which stages actually count

| Stage | Marks | Counts towards merit? |
|---|---|---|
| Preliminary examination | 70 | No, screening only |
| Main examination, objective | 300 | Yes |
| Interview | As notified | Yes |
| Pre-recruitment medical examination | Qualifying | No |

Two features of that structure are worth acting on.

The preliminary examination is pure screening. Its 70 marks do not enter the final merit list. So the correct objective in prelims is to clear it with a comfortable margin, and any effort spent pushing a safe prelims score higher is effort taken from the mains, where selection is actually decided.

Final merit rests on the main examination and the interview together. That makes the mains the substantive project and the interview a genuine component rather than a formality, which is different from recruitments like IBPS Clerk where the mains score alone decides everything.

## No negative marking, in either paper

This is unusual and it changes attempt strategy completely.

There is no negative marking in the preliminary examination or in the main examination. Nothing is deducted for a wrong answer.

Work through what that means. An unattempted question scores zero with certainty. A guessed answer among four options carries a one in four chance of scoring and costs nothing. There is no scenario in which leaving a question blank is the better choice.

So the target in both papers is to finish with every question answered. Reserve the closing minute of each section to fill anything unattempted, choosing at random where necessary.

Candidates arriving from banking examinations find this genuinely hard to do. IBPS and SBI papers penalise wrong answers at 0.25, and months of training yourself to skip uncertain questions builds a reflex that actively costs marks here. It is worth rehearsing in mocks rather than deciding on the day, because the habit does not switch off under pressure.

## Eligibility

**Age.** 21 to 30 years, with relaxation for reserved categories as specified in the notification. That upper limit of 30 is narrower than most state civil services and comparable to the banking recruitments, so it is worth checking against your own position early.

**Education, generalist stream.** A bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognised Indian university or institution. No specific subject requirement, which makes this open to graduates from any background.

**Education, specialist streams.** LIC recruits AAOs in specialist categories alongside the generalist stream, with professional qualifications required: Chartered Accountancy, Company Secretaryship, actuarial qualifications and similar, depending on the category notified.

That specialist provision is worth flagging for candidates who hold such a qualification. A CA or an actuarial student competing in a specialist category is competing against a much smaller field of similarly qualified candidates rather than against the entire graduate population, which changes the odds substantially. The same qualification that counts for nothing in the generalist stream is the whole advantage in a specialist one.

## What the paper covers

The examination follows the pattern familiar from banking and insurance recruitment, with an insurance-specific layer.

**Reasoning ability.** Series, analogies, coding and decoding, blood relations, directions, seating arrangements, puzzles, syllogisms, statement and assumption, and data sufficiency.

**Quantitative aptitude.** Arithmetic including percentages, ratio and proportion, averages, profit and loss, simple and compound interest, time and work, time and distance, along with number series, simplification, quadratic equations and data interpretation.

**English language.** Reading comprehension, cloze tests, error spotting, sentence improvement, para jumbles and vocabulary in context.

**General knowledge, current affairs and insurance awareness.** This is where the recruitment differs from a general banking examination. Alongside standard current affairs and general awareness, expect insurance-specific material: the structure of the Indian insurance industry, the role of the regulator, types of insurance products and terminology, the difference between life and general insurance, and current developments in the sector.

Insurance awareness is the section that rewards targeted study most, because it is a defined body of material that most candidates preparing on general banking content will not have covered. It is the cheapest differentiator available on this paper.

## Preparing for it

**Build the common base first.** Reasoning, quantitative aptitude and English are shared with every banking and insurance recruitment, so this work serves multiple applications. If you are already preparing for IBPS or SBI, most of the foundation is done.

**Add insurance awareness deliberately.** A few weeks of focused reading on the Indian insurance sector, its regulator, product categories and terminology produces marks that general preparation does not reach. Treat it as a distinct project rather than an extension of banking awareness.

**Practise without the skipping reflex.** Take timed mocks and force yourself to answer every question, since that is the correct behaviour on a paper with no penalty and it needs training if your habits come from negative-marking exams.

**Prepare the interview from the start.** Because the interview carries weight in the final merit, being able to discuss why insurance, why LIC, and what you understand about the industry is part of the preparation rather than an afterthought. A candidate who can talk sensibly about the sector interviews far better than one who has only memorised facts about it.

**Work the mains as the priority.** Prelims is screening at 70 marks that do not count. Mains at 300 marks does. Allocate accordingly.

## What the job involves

An Assistant Administrative Officer is a Class I officer position in LIC, which is a different proposition from a clerical or assistant grade.

The work covers policy administration and underwriting, claims processing and settlement, branch and divisional administration, supervision of staff, agency management including the network of agents through which LIC distributes, marketing and business development, and the accounting and compliance work attached to a regulated financial institution.

Specialist AAOs work within their discipline: chartered accountants in accounts and finance functions, actuarial specialists on product pricing and reserving, and so on.

Postings are across LIC's national network of divisional and branch offices, so transfer liability applies. Progression runs through LIC's own officer grades, from Assistant Administrative Officer upward through Administrative Officer, Assistant Divisional Manager and higher management grades, on the basis of service, performance and internal selection.

## How this compares with the alternatives

For a graduate weighing options, the honest comparison matters more than the headline.

Against **banking recruitment**, LIC AAO pays substantially more at entry than an IBPS or SBI Probationary Officer. The syllabus overlaps heavily, so a candidate preparing for banking can add LIC AAO for the cost of insurance awareness. Our [banking exam calendar](/blog/banking-exam-calendar-2026) covers how to fit multiple applications into a season.

Against **UPSC Civil Services and state PCS**, LIC AAO pays more at entry and asks far less: one preparation base rather than a multi-year commitment, a narrower syllabus, and a selection process measured in months. What it does not offer is the statutory authority, public role or career ceiling of the administrative services. That is a genuine trade rather than a straightforward win either way, and it depends on what you want from a career. Our [government job salary comparison](/blog/government-job-salary-comparison-2026) sets out how pay mechanisms differ across these routes.

Against **private sector employment**, the package is competitive at entry and carries the security, medical cover and pension provision of a large public sector institution.

The reason to sit this examination is straightforward: it is one of the best-paid graduate entry points in the public sector, the preparation overlaps with recruitments you are probably already targeting, and it attracts less attention than its pay warrants.

## Insurance awareness: what to actually study

Since this is the section that differentiates scores and the one general banking preparation misses, it deserves specifics rather than a note to study it.

**The industry structure.** How Indian insurance is organised: the split between life and general insurance, the position of LIC as the largest life insurer, the private life insurers, the public and private general insurers, and the reinsurance layer.

**The regulator.** The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India, what it does, how it licenses insurers and intermediaries, and the broad shape of the regulatory framework insurers operate under.

**Product categories.** Term insurance, endowment and money-back policies, whole life, unit linked insurance plans, annuities and pension products on the life side; motor, health, fire, marine, travel and liability on the general side. What each is for, and the basic distinction between protection and savings-linked products.

**Core terminology.** Premium, sum assured, maturity and death benefit, surrender value, paid-up value, grace period, lapse and revival, rider, nomination and assignment, free-look period, underwriting, claim settlement ratio, and the principles of insurable interest and indemnity.

**Distribution.** How policies actually reach customers: individual agents, corporate agents, bancassurance, brokers and direct online channels. LIC's agent network is central to its business, and an AAO works with it.

**Government insurance schemes.** Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana, Ayushman Bharat, crop insurance under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana and the Atal Pension Yojana. These recur in questions and they connect to material a candidate following government schemes already knows.

**Current developments.** Regulatory changes, sector growth figures, insurance penetration and density in India relative to other economies, and notable industry events of the preceding year.

That list is finite. A few weeks of reading covers it, and it is the portion of the paper where preparation converts most directly into marks.

## A realistic preparation timeline

Working from an August notification, with a preliminary examination likely within a couple of months, the sequence looks like this.

**Immediately.** Establish where you stand with a timed mock across reasoning, quantitative aptitude and English. Without a baseline you are guessing at where the effort belongs, and the three sections diverge widely between candidates, so the allocation that works for someone else will not be the allocation that works for you.

**First three weeks.** The weakest of the three core sections, worked daily with timed practice sets rather than theory reading. Aptitude improves through volume, not through understanding more.

**Running throughout.** Current affairs, daily, from a newspaper plus a monthly compilation.

**Weeks three to six.** Insurance awareness as a distinct block, working through the material above. This is also the point to begin thinking about the interview, since the same knowledge serves both.

**From week four.** Full-length timed mocks at prelims pattern, with the explicit discipline of answering every question, since there is no penalty. Track how many you leave blank and drive it to zero.

**After prelims.** Mains preparation is a step up in both scope and difficulty at 300 marks, and the gap between prelims and mains is where that work happens. Candidates who treat clearing prelims as the achievement rather than the entry point lose here.

**Throughout.** Interview preparation as a slow background task: reading about the sector, forming views you can defend, and being able to explain your own background and motivation coherently. Because the interview counts towards final merit here, an hour a week on this from the start is worth more than a fortnight of scrambling after the mains result.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is the LIC AAO salary in 2026?**
The basic pay is Rs 88,635 in a scale running to Rs 1,69,025. With house rent allowance, city compensatory allowance, travel and petrol allowances, the package in an A-class city works out to approximately Rs 1,26,000 a month. That is higher at entry than an IAS officer, who starts at Pay Level 10 with a basic of Rs 56,100 and around Rs 1,00,000 in hand in a metro.

**Is LIC AAO really better paid than an IAS officer at entry?**
On the entry package, yes. LIC operates its own pay structure as a public sector insurer, revised through its own settlements rather than the central Pay Commission matrix, which produces a higher entry figure. What an IAS post offers instead is statutory authority, a public role and a career ceiling reaching the most senior positions in government, none of which LIC AAO provides. The comparison is a genuine trade rather than a straight win.

**When is the LIC AAO 2026 notification?**
Expected in August 2026 on licindia.in, and not released at the time of writing. Because it is not out, vacancy counts and exact dates are not established, so any specific figure circulating now is a projection. Watch licindia.in directly, since LIC publishes there and the details are fixed in that document.

**Is there negative marking in LIC AAO?**
No, in neither the preliminary nor the main examination. Nothing is deducted for a wrong answer, which means an unattempted question scores zero with certainty while a guess among four options carries a one in four chance and costs nothing. You should finish both papers with every question answered, and reserve the closing minute of each section to fill any blanks.

**Do LIC AAO prelims marks count in the final merit?**
No. The preliminary examination at 70 marks is purely a screening stage. Final merit rests on the main examination at 300 marks together with the interview. The practical implication is to clear prelims with a comfortable margin rather than maximising the score, and to direct the bulk of preparation at the mains where selection is decided.

**What is the age limit for LIC AAO?**
21 to 30 years, with relaxation for reserved categories as specified in the notification. That ceiling of 30 is narrower than most state civil services, which commonly run to 37 or higher, so candidates approaching that age should check their position early rather than assuming a wider band.

**What qualification is needed for LIC AAO?**
For the generalist stream, a bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognised Indian university, with no subject restriction. Specialist streams require professional qualifications such as Chartered Accountancy, Company Secretaryship or actuarial qualifications, depending on the categories notified in the cycle.

**Should I apply in a specialist category if I have a CA?**
If you hold a qualifying professional qualification, seriously consider it. A specialist category means competing against a much smaller field of similarly qualified candidates rather than the entire graduate population, which changes the odds substantially. The same qualification that counts for nothing in the generalist stream is the whole advantage in a specialist one.

**What is insurance awareness and how much does it matter?**
A section covering the structure of the Indian insurance industry, the role of the regulator, types of insurance products and terminology, the distinction between life and general insurance, and current sector developments. It matters more than its share of marks suggests, because it is a defined body of material that candidates preparing on general banking content will not have covered, which makes it the cheapest way to differentiate your score on this paper.

**Can I prepare for LIC AAO alongside banking exams?**
Yes, and it is the efficient approach. Reasoning, quantitative aptitude and English are shared with every banking and insurance recruitment, so a candidate already preparing for IBPS or SBI has most of the foundation. The additions are insurance awareness and unlearning the skip-uncertain-questions habit that negative marking trains, since this paper has no penalty.

It carries weight in the final merit alongside the mains, unlike recruitments such as IBPS Clerk where the written score alone decides. That means preparing to discuss why insurance, why LIC, and what you understand about the sector is part of the preparation rather than something to handle after the result. It is a Class I officer position covering policy administration and underwriting, claims processing and settlement, branch and divisional administration, staff supervision, agency management across LIC's agent network, marketing and business development, and the accounting and compliance work of a regulated financial institution. Specialist officers work within their discipline. Postings span LIC's national network, so transfer liability applies, and progression runs through LIC's own officer grades.

title: IBPS PO vs SBI PO 2026: Which Banking Exam Should You Target?
description: IBPS PO or SBI PO: which banking exam gives you the better career? A side-by-side comparison of salary, difficulty, number of banks, selection process.
author: Mahitosh Dey
tags: sbi po salary vs ibps po salary
content:
## IBPS PO vs SBI PO — An Honest Comparison for 2026

This question comes up constantly in banking exam preparation communities, and there's no clean universal answer — because the right choice depends entirely on your situation, your goals, and honestly, your preference for which bank you'd like to work in.

Let's go through every important dimension, side by side.

## The Basic Difference in One Line

**SBI PO** = One exam, one bank (State Bank of India).
**IBPS PO** = One exam, eleven banks (Punjab National Bank, Bank of Baroda, Canara Bank, Union Bank, Bank of India, Central Bank, Indian Bank, UCO Bank, Bank of Maharashtra, Punjab & Sind Bank, Indian Overseas Bank).

## Exam Dates 2026

| Stage | SBI PO 2026 | IBPS PO 2026 |
|---|---|---|
| Notification | June 2026 (Expected) | July 2026 (Expected) |
| Prelims | August 1–2, 2026 | **August 22–23, 2026 (Confirmed)** |
| Mains | September 12, 2026 | **October 4, 2026 (Confirmed)** |
| GE + Interview / Interview | Oct–Nov 2026 | Nov–Dec 2026 |

SBI PO comes before IBPS PO in the calendar, so many candidates appear for both. If you clear SBI PO, great. If not, IBPS PO gives you another chance in the same preparation cycle.

## Salary — They're Close, but Not Identical

Both start at a **basic pay of ₹36,000 per month**. But the total package differs slightly.

| | SBI PO | IBPS PO |
|---|---|---|
| Basic Pay | ₹36,000/month | ₹36,000/month |
| Gross (metro city) | ₹52,000–₹58,000/month | ₹52,000–₹57,000/month |
| Annual CTC | ~₹8–8.5 lakh | ~₹7.5–8 lakh |

SBI has slightly better allowances (Special Allowance, CCA, etc.) in certain postings, which is why the SBI PO gross is marginally higher. But at the entry level, both are very close.

## Exam Difficulty — SBI PO is Harder

This is not a controversial opinion — SBI PO consistently sets tougher Mains papers than IBPS PO.

**SBI PO Mains:** The DI and Reasoning sets are more complex. The English section has longer RC passages. And there's a Descriptive English paper worth **50 marks** — essay + letter, manually evaluated.

**IBPS PO Mains:** Also tough, but slightly more predictable in terms of question types. Descriptive paper is only **25 marks**.

**SBI PO also has a Group Exercise** in Stage 3, which IBPS PO does not. IBPS PO goes straight to Interview.

If you can crack SBI PO Mains, IBPS PO Mains will feel more manageable — not easier, but more familiar.

## Career Growth — SBI Has the Edge

SBI is the largest bank in India, with over 22,000 branches and a global presence. The career progression within SBI is faster in certain grades and more structured. An SBI PO can become an Assistant Manager in 1-2 years, then Deputy Manager, then Manager, and so on.

IBPS PO officers join one of the 11 participating banks. Career growth depends on the specific bank. Banks like PNB and Bank of Baroda have robust internal promotion systems, while some smaller banks may be slower.

**For long-term career:** SBI is generally considered more prestigious, with better internal transfer options, international postings, and access to specialized roles (forex, wealth management, treasury).

## Number of Vacancies — IBPS PO Has More

Because 11 banks participate in IBPS PO, the total vacancies are typically much higher than SBI PO.

- **IBPS PO vacancies (typical cycle):** 3,000–5,000 posts across 11 banks
- **SBI PO vacancies (typical cycle):** 2,000–3,000 posts

More vacancies = slightly lower competition per seat with IBPS PO. This matters if you're on the borderline.

## Selection Process Comparison

| Stage | SBI PO | IBPS PO |
|---|---|---|
| Prelims | 100 marks, qualifying | 100 marks, qualifying |
| Mains (Objective) | 200 marks | 200 marks |
| Mains (Descriptive) | 50 marks | 25 marks |
| Stage 3 | Group Exercise (20) + Interview (30) | Interview only (100 marks) |
| Final Merit | Mains + GE + Interview | Mains 80% + Interview 20% |

The SBI PO Group Exercise is an additional elimination round that IBPS PO doesn't have. If you're not confident in group discussions, this can be nerve-wracking. But it also gives you one more chance to impress if your Mains score is average.

## Should You Apply for Both?

**Yes — if your preparation level allows it.** The syllabus overlap between SBI PO and IBPS PO is around 85-90%. Most of what you study for one is directly useful for the other. The main adjustments are:

- For SBI PO: Extra practice on harder DI sets and Descriptive English (50 marks)
- For IBPS PO: Slightly lower Descriptive effort needed (25 marks)

If you start preparing from June-July 2026, you can realistically target both. SBI PO Prelims is in August; IBPS PO Prelims is also in August (but a week later). You'd appear in SBI PO, get exam experience, and then give IBPS PO.

## Who Should Prioritise SBI PO?

- You want to work specifically in SBI
- You don't mind a harder exam and are confident in your Mains preparation
- Long-term career growth and brand name matter to you
- You're comfortable with Group Discussion situations

## Who Should Prioritise IBPS PO?

- You want flexibility — 11 banks give you more options for preferred posting location
- You want higher vacancy count (better odds)
- You're not sure about a Group Exercise round
- Your banking awareness is strong enough for the Mains but you want a slightly less brutal exam

## Final Take

The honest answer: if you're serious about banking, **prepare for SBI PO and apply for both**. SBI PO gives you the tougher challenge; IBPS PO gives you the backup. Most people who clear SBI PO would have cleared IBPS PO too. Very few people who can't crack SBI PO would have cleared IBPS PO in the same cycle — but it does happen, especially at the Mains level.

Don't choose between them. Use one to prepare better for the other.

title: UPSC vs SSC 2026: Which Exam is Right for You? Guide
description: Choose between UPSC and SSC for your govt job goals. This 2026 guide compares prep time, difficulty, salary, job profile, and best-fit candidate profile.
author: Mahitosh Dey
tags: upsc or ssc which is better
content:
## UPSC vs SSC: choosing the right path in 2026

At some point, almost every government job aspirant faces this question: should I go for UPSC Civil Services or SSC CGL? Both lead to central government careers. Both offer good salaries and job security. But they are fundamentally different in terms of the preparation commitment required, the posts you get, and the kind of life you'll lead after selection.

Let's go through this honestly, without the hype that coaching institutes typically bring to this comparison.

## The core difference

**UPSC Civil Services** (IAS, IPS, IFS, and 24 other Group A services) is an all-India competitive exam where roughly 10 lakh candidates compete for approximately 1,000 seats, of which only about 180 go to IAS. Preparation takes 2-5 years on average. The posts are the most powerful in the Indian administrative system.

**SSC CGL** (Staff Selection Commission Combined Graduate Level) recruits for approximately 40+ different posts across central government ministries and departments, including Income Tax Inspector, Excise Inspector, Central Excise Officer, Audit Officer, Statistical Investigator, Sub-Inspector (CBI), and many more. Vacancies are in the thousands every cycle. Preparation can yield results in 6-18 months for a focused candidate.

## Exam structure

### UPSC Civil Services
- **Prelims:** 2 objective papers (GS Paper I + CSAT). Qualifying in nature.
- **Mains:** 9 written papers: 4 GS papers, 1 Essay, 2 Optional Subject papers, 1 Indian Language, 1 English. Approximately 1750 marks.
- **Interview (Personality Test):** 275 marks.
- **Total timeline:** Notification to final result takes approximately 12 months per cycle.

### SSC CGL
- **Tier 1:** 100 MCQs covering GK, Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, English. 60 minutes.
- **Tier 2:** 3 papers. Paper 1 (Mathematical Abilities + Reasoning + English + General Awareness + Computer Knowledge, 390 merit marks, ~3 hours), Paper 2 (Statistics, for JSO posts, 2 hours), Paper 3 (Finance & Economics, for AAO posts, 2 hours). Note: The Computer Knowledge Test section within Paper 1 is qualifying in nature and not counted in merit.
- **No Interview** for most posts (removed in 2016). Selection is purely merit-based on Tier 1 + Tier 2 marks.
- **Total timeline:** Notification to result takes 6-12 months typically.

## Preparation time: the honest reality

**UPSC:** The average successful candidate makes 2-4 attempts. First-timers who clear in one attempt are rare. Most serious aspirants spend 2-3 years in full-time preparation. The breadth of the syllabus, history, geography, economy, polity, science, current affairs, essays, is enormous. Optional subjects add another layer of specialization.

**SSC CGL:** A focused candidate with a decent educational background can clear Tier 1 in 3-6 months of serious preparation. Tier 2 requires additional 2-3 months. Many working professionals clear SSC CGL while preparing after office hours.

This time difference is the single most important factor in the decision. Every year you spend preparing for UPSC without clearing it is a year without income (unless you're working). That's a significant opportunity cost.

## Posts and job profiles

### What You Get with UPSC

If you crack IAS: Sub-Divisional Magistrate → District Magistrate → Divisional Commissioner → Principal Secretary → Secretary to Government of India. Maximum authority, maximum responsibility, maximum impact.

If you crack IPS: ASP → SP → DIG → IG → DGP. Law enforcement leadership.

If you crack Group A Central Services (IRS, IDAS, IRTS, etc.): Senior positions in Income Tax, Customs, Defence Accounts, Railways, and other central departments.

### What You Get with SSC CGL

**Income Tax Inspector (CPC):** Field enforcement, tax audit, TDS verification. Pay Level 7 (₹44,900 basic).

**Excise Inspector / Central Excise Officer:** GST enforcement, anti-smuggling operations. Exciting fieldwork, uniform job.

**Sub-Inspector CBI:** Investigations at the country's premier investigative agency. One of the most sought-after SSC CGL posts.

**Audit and Accounts Officer:** Office-based work in CAG/CGDA. Regular hours, steady career.

**Statistical Investigator (Ministry of Statistics):** Research-oriented role for candidates with Statistics background.

## Salary comparison at entry level

| Post | Basic Pay | Gross Monthly (Approx.) |
|---|---|---|
| IAS (entry, Pay Level 10) | ₹56,100 | ₹95,000 to ₹1,10,000 |
| IPS (entry, Pay Level 10) | ₹56,100 | ₹95,000 to ₹1,10,000 |
| Income Tax Inspector (SSC CGL) | ₹44,900 | ₹72,000 to ₹80,000 |
| Excise Inspector (SSC CGL) | ₹44,900 | ₹72,000 to ₹80,000 |
| Sub-Inspector CBI (SSC CGL) | ₹35,400 | ₹60,000 to ₹70,000 |
| Audit Officer (SSC CGL) | ₹47,600 | ₹75,000 to ₹85,000 |

The IAS/IPS package is higher, but the difference narrows when you factor in work hours and stress levels. An Income Tax Inspector with a predictable 9-5 schedule may have a better quality of life than a District Magistrate handling 18-hour workdays during elections or disasters.

## Who should choose UPSC?

- You have a genuine interest in public administration and governance, not just the designation
- You are prepared to invest 3-5 years of serious, focused preparation
- You can sustain yourself financially during the preparation period
- You can handle failure, reset, and try again
- You want the highest administrative authority in the country

## Who should choose SSC CGL?

- You want a good government job in a reasonable timeframe (1-2 years of preparation)
- You want stability, regular hours, and a central government lifestyle without the gruelling UPSC journey
- You don't necessarily need to be a district magistrate, and you're fine being an Income Tax Inspector or an Audit Officer
- You want to start earning sooner and build your life while working
- You're already working and preparing part-time

## Can you prepare for both?

Yes, with limits. The Prelims-level preparation (GK, Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, English) overlaps between UPSC Prelims and SSC CGL Tier 1. Many aspirants begin with SSC CGL as a "backup" while building toward UPSC.

The problem comes at the Mains level. UPSC Mains requires deep, analytical writing on 9 papers. SSC Tier 2 is objective. They require very different mental modes. Trying to actively prepare for UPSC Mains AND SSC Tier 2 simultaneously is not recommended, one will suffer.

**Practical approach:** Clear SSC CGL first (get a job, get income), then prepare for UPSC with financial security. This is what thousands of successful IAS officers have done, they joined as SSC officers first.

## What to actually ask yourself

It's not "which exam pays more" or "which is more prestigious." The real question is: **what do you actually want to do for the next 30 years?**

If administration, governance, and public service genuinely excite you, go for UPSC. If you want a good government career with a manageable preparation journey and a stable life sooner, SSC CGL is not a consolation prize. It's a genuinely excellent career.

Both paths are valid. The worst thing is to spend 5 years half-heartedly chasing UPSC without clearing it and then scrambling for SSC without adequate preparation either. Decide early, commit fully.


## Attempt limits, the difference nobody weighs properly

This is the structural difference that should carry more weight in the decision than it usually does.

UPSC caps attempts. Six for the general category, nine for Other Backward Classes, and no cap up to the age ceiling for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. Appearing in the preliminary examination consumes an attempt, while applying without appearing does not.

SSC CGL imposes no attempt limit at all. Eligibility is governed by age alone, so a candidate can sit it every year they remain within the band.

Read together with the age limits, the two examinations offer very different runways. A general category candidate starting UPSC at 24 has six attempts and an age ceiling at 32. The same candidate has roughly eight years of SSC CGL attempts with no cap on how many they use.

That asymmetry matters most for candidates who are uncertain. A capped, high-difficulty examination punishes indecision, because attempts spent while you were half-committed are gone. An uncapped one does not.

## The optional subject, and what it really costs

UPSC Mains includes an optional subject worth 500 marks across two papers. SSC CGL has nothing equivalent.

Five hundred marks is close to a fifth of the 1750 written total, more than any single General Studies paper. That alone makes it significant, but the real cost is time. An optional subject is a university-level syllabus studied to a standard where you can write analytically about it under examination conditions, and most candidates spend several months on it before they are competitive.

Candidates comparing preparation timelines frequently leave this out. The gap between UPSC and SSC CGL preparation is not simply that UPSC is harder. It is that UPSC contains an entire additional subject that SSC does not, plus a descriptive writing skill that objective preparation never builds.

If you are weighing the two on effort, count the optional as a separate project rather than folding it into general preparation.

## What the work actually looks like

Comparisons dwell on pay and status and skip the thing you will experience daily for decades.

An IAS officer in district administration handles revenue matters, magistracy, law and order coordination, election duties, scheme implementation and whatever crisis arrives that week. The authority is real and so is the unpredictability. Hours are long, transfers are frequent, and public and political pressure is a permanent feature.

An Income Tax Inspector or Excise Inspector works within a defined functional area, with investigation and enforcement components depending on the posting. The work is substantive and the hours are more predictable than district administration, though field roles carry their own demands.

An Assistant Section Officer in a ministry works on files, policy inputs and coordination in a secretariat environment. It is desk work in the centre of government, which suits some people well and bores others.

An Assistant Audit Officer examines government spending. The work is analytical, largely predictable, and carries a professional character closer to accountancy than to administration.

None of these is better. They are different jobs, and a candidate who wants one would be unhappy in another regardless of which examination they cleared.

## The financial reality of a long attempt

Nobody enjoys discussing this and it decides more outcomes than aptitude does.

A multi-year UPSC attempt has a cost: living expenses, coaching if you use it, materials, and the earnings you are not making. For a candidate supported by family this is absorbable. For one who needs to contribute to household income it may not be.

SSC CGL, banking and railway examinations have shorter cycles and higher selection ratios, which means a realistic prospect of employment within a year or two rather than a possibility after four.

The strategy that works for most people in the second position is to secure a post first and prepare afterwards. A candidate working as an Income Tax Inspector who prepares for UPSC in the evenings has income, security and no deadline pressure. A candidate with none of those is making every attempt under financial strain, which affects performance directly.

There is no honour in the harder path if it breaks you financially. The candidates who clear UPSC after several attempts are disproportionately those who could afford several attempts.

## The third option most comparisons ignore

Framing this as UPSC against SSC CGL leaves out state public service commissions, and for many candidates they are the better answer.

State PSCs recruit Deputy Collectors, Deputy Superintendents of Police and equivalent posts through examinations structured much like UPSC, with prelims, descriptive mains and an interview. The work is district administration within one state.

Two features make them worth serious consideration. Age limits generally run higher, frequently to 40, which keeps the route open for candidates who have aged out of UPSC. And competition, while heavy, is lower than the national examination because the candidate pool is state-scoped.

The preparation overlaps substantially with UPSC, since general studies is shared, though state-specific history, geography, polity and current affairs form a body of material that earns nothing at UPSC and everything at the state level.

A candidate who wants district administration specifically, and is willing to work within one state, may reach it faster through the state commission than through UPSC. That is not a lesser outcome. A Sub Divisional Magistrate exercises real authority regardless of which examination placed them there.
## Common mistakes in making this choice

Choosing on prestige rather than on the work. The designation lasts a moment at a family gathering; the job lasts thirty years. Candidates who pick the examination people respect, rather than the work they want, are the ones who arrive at a post and wonder why it does not feel as expected.

Treating SSC CGL as a consolation. It is competitive enough to require genuine preparation, and candidates who approach it with leftover effort after a failed UPSC attempt generally do not clear it either. Posts like Assistant Audit Officer and Income Tax Inspector are substantial careers chosen deliberately by people who wanted them.

Underestimating the descriptive transition. A candidate strong at objective papers is not automatically ready for nine descriptive papers, and the gap is a skill built over months rather than a matter of knowing more.

Ignoring the attempt cap while drifting. UPSC attempts spent during a half-committed year are gone permanently. If you are going to attempt it, attempt it properly; if you are not ready to commit, sitting the prelims casually is an expensive way to find out.

Forgetting that both examinations are winnable at once early on. The prelims-level foundation is shared, so a candidate in their first year of preparation loses nothing by keeping both open and specialising later.

Comparing entry salaries alone. Entry pay understates the UPSC trajectory and overstates the difference at the start. Career progression, not starting basic, is where the two genuinely diverge.

Assuming coaching decides the outcome. It provides structure for those who need it and it does not substitute for daily independent study, which is what actually separates candidates in both examinations.

## A practical decision framework

If you are stuck, work through these in order rather than agonising over the comparison as a whole.

Start with what you want to do daily. District administration, enforcement work, secretariat policy work and audit are different jobs. Pick the work first, then the examination that leads to it, because the examination is a means and the job is the point.

Then check your runway honestly. How many years can you afford to prepare without income, and how many attempts does your age band allow? A candidate with two years and a general category age of 28 is in a different position from one with five years at 22, and the same advice does not serve both.

Then decide whether you can build the descriptive skill. UPSC Mains rewards structured writing under time. Some candidates take to it quickly and some struggle for years. Write a few practice answers before committing a multi-year plan to an examination built on a skill you have not tested.

Then look at state PSCs against your own state. If district administration is what you want and you are content within one state, that route may be shorter than the national one.

Finally, keep both open in the first year if you genuinely cannot decide. The shared foundation costs you nothing, and a year of preparation will tell you more about your own aptitude and appetite than any comparison article can.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is UPSC harder than SSC CGL?**

Yes, by most measures. UPSC Civil Services has a far lower selection ratio, a descriptive main examination across nine papers, an optional subject worth 500 marks, and a personality test carrying 275. SSC CGL is objective throughout with a shorter cycle. That said, SSC CGL is genuinely competitive and the gap is in scale and depth rather than one being easy.

**Can I prepare for UPSC and SSC CGL together?**

The general studies foundation overlaps substantially, so early preparation serves both. They diverge sharply later: UPSC needs answer writing, an optional subject and far greater depth, while SSC CGL needs speed and accuracy on objective questions. Most candidates who attempt both treat SSC CGL as the primary target and UPSC as the stretch, or prepare for UPSC and sit SSC CGL as a floor.

**Which pays more, UPSC or SSC CGL?**

SSC CGL posts at Pay Level 8 start higher than many people assume, and the entry gap against UPSC posts is smaller than reputation suggests. The difference is progression: UPSC Civil Services posts advance to positions with authority and pay that SSC CGL posts do not reach. Comparing entry salaries alone misses the point of the comparison.

**How long does UPSC preparation take compared with SSC?**

For UPSC Civil Services, a year is the minimum most candidates need and two is common, with many successful candidates taking multiple attempts. For SSC CGL, six months to a year of consistent work is a realistic first attempt for a graduate. That difference in commitment is the practical factor most worth weighing.

**Should I choose SSC CGL if I fail UPSC?**

Treating SSC CGL as a fallback tends to produce poor results in both, because it is competitive enough to require real preparation rather than leftover effort. A better framing is to decide what you want the work to be. SSC CGL posts are substantial careers in their own right, and candidates who choose them deliberately generally do better than those who arrive at them by default.

**What is the age limit for UPSC and SSC CGL?**

UPSC Civil Services runs 21 to 32 for the general category, extended to 35 for Other Backward Classes and 37 for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. SSC CGL varies by post, broadly 18 to 32, with standard relaxation. UPSC additionally caps attempts, which SSC does not.

**Does UPSC have an attempt limit?**

Yes. Six attempts for the general category and nine for Other Backward Classes, with no cap up to the age ceiling for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. Appearing in the preliminary examination counts as an attempt while applying without appearing does not. SSC CGL imposes no attempt limit.

**Which exam is better for work life balance?**

SSC CGL posts in ministries and central offices generally offer more predictable hours. UPSC Civil Services postings in district administration and police services involve long and unpredictable hours, particularly in the early years. Candidates who value stability of routine should weigh that seriously, because it is a structural feature rather than a temporary phase.

**Do I need an optional subject for SSC CGL?**

No. SSC CGL has no optional subject. UPSC Civil Services requires one, worth 500 marks across two papers, which is close to a fifth of the written total and represents months of dedicated preparation. That single difference accounts for much of the gap in preparation time between the two.

**Can I switch from SSC preparation to UPSC later?**

Yes, and the general studies foundation carries over usefully. What you would need to add is answer writing, an optional subject and considerably greater depth across the syllabus. The reverse switch is easier, since a UPSC candidate is generally well prepared for SSC CGL apart from the speed and accuracy practice the objective format rewards.

title: How to Clear IBPS Clerk 2026 in Your First Attempt: Complete
description: A practical, honest guide to clearing IBPS Clerk 2026 in your very first attempt: understanding what's different about Clerk vs PO, section-wise strategy.
author: Mahitosh Dey
content:
## How to Clear IBPS Clerk 2026 in Your First Attempt

IBPS Clerk is often dismissed as "the easier banking exam" — and in some ways, it is. The Prelims is simpler than IBPS PO, there's no Group Exercise, and there's no interview. But that also means hundreds of thousands of serious candidates appear for it, and the Mains cutoffs can be surprisingly high.

Clearing IBPS Clerk in your first attempt is absolutely possible. In fact, it is one of the best-designed exams to crack on the first try if you prepare smartly. Here's exactly how.

## Know What Makes IBPS Clerk Different

Before getting into strategy, understand three things that make IBPS Clerk unique:

**1. No interview.** Your Mains marks alone determine your bank allotment. There's no redemption round if you score average in Mains. Everything rides on one exam.

**2. Language requirement.** You must have studied the official language of the state you're applying to in Class 10, 12, or graduation. If you're applying for a Tamil Nadu bank and you haven't studied Tamil — you're ineligible. Check this before applying.

**3. Local language in Mains.** The "General English" section in Mains can be replaced by the regional language section in some states for candidates who opt for that language. Know your option before you sit for the exam.

## The Two-Stage Process

**Prelims (October 10–11, 2026 — CONFIRMED):** 100 questions, 60 minutes. English (30), Numerical Ability (35), Reasoning (35). Qualifying only — these marks don't count in merit.

**Mains (December 27, 2026 — CONFIRMED):** 190 questions, 160 minutes. Four sections:

| Section | Questions | Marks | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| General/Financial Awareness | 50 | 50 | 35 min |
| General English | 40 | 40 | 35 min |
| Reasoning Ability & Computer Aptitude | 50 | 60 | 45 min |
| Quantitative Aptitude | 50 | 50 | 45 min |

No descriptive paper. No interview. These 190 questions in 160 minutes determine your fate.

## The Most Common Mistake — Ignoring General Awareness

Most candidates prepare heavily for Reasoning and Quantitative Aptitude but treat General/Financial Awareness as an afterthought. This is a mistake.

General/Financial Awareness carries **50 marks out of 200** in IBPS Clerk Mains. And since all candidates typically score similarly on Reasoning and Quantitative Aptitude (because they've all practiced from the same books), it's the GK/Awareness section where ranks are actually decided.

A candidate who scores 38/50 in GK has a 15-mark advantage over one who scores 23/50 — and that gap is nearly impossible to make up in Reasoning or Quant alone.

**What to study for GK/Financial Awareness:**
- RBI — repo rate (check latest RBI circular for current rate), reverse repo, CRR, SLR (18%), monetary policy
- Banking schemes — PM Jan Dhan Yojana, Mudra Loan, Stand Up India, PM CARES
- Government economic schemes — PM Kisan, PM SVANidhi, Atmanirbhar Bharat
- Banking terms — NPA, SARFAESI Act, IBC, CIBIL score, NEFT, RTGS, IMPS limits
- Financial market basics — SEBI, stock exchange, mutual funds, bonds
- Current affairs — last 6 months, with focus on banking and economy news
- Important appointments — RBI Governor, Finance Minister, SBI Chairman, and other key positions

**Daily habit that makes a difference:** Spend 25-30 minutes every day on banking current affairs using GKToday or AffairsCloud. Do this from July through December — that's the entire preparation period.

## Reasoning & Computer Aptitude — 50 questions, 60 marks

Reasoning in IBPS Clerk Mains is harder than in Prelims but not as complex as IBPS PO Mains. The difficulty sits in the middle. Puzzles dominate the paper — expect 3-4 puzzle sets of 4-5 questions each.

**What to focus on:**
- Seating arrangement (linear: 1 row and 2 rows; circular; floor-based)
- Puzzles (scheduling, box puzzles, day-date puzzles)
- Blood relations, direction sense, coding-decoding (simpler level)
- Syllogisms, inequalities (usually 3-5 questions, quick to attempt)

**Computer Aptitude (part of this section):** MS Office basics, internet terminology, hardware (CPU, RAM, ROM, input/output devices), software, networking abbreviations (LAN, WAN, HTTPS, DNS). Typically 5-8 questions. Don't spend more than 4-5 days on this.

**Strategy tip:** In the 45-minute time slot, spend the first 20 minutes on puzzles. If a puzzle is taking too long, skip it and return later. Syllogisms and inequalities are the fastest questions — attempt these first.

## Quantitative Aptitude — 50 questions, 50 marks

Arithmetic and Data Interpretation split this section roughly 50:50.

**Arithmetic topics:** Number series, simplification/approximation, percentage, profit and loss, ratio and proportion, averages, time and work, pipes and cisterns, simple and compound interest, speed and distance. These require clean calculation speed.

**Data Interpretation:** 2-3 DI sets of 4-5 questions each. Bar charts, tables, pie charts, and line graphs are standard. Caselet DI (paragraph-based) appears occasionally in Clerk Mains.

**Strategy tip:** Attempt Arithmetic questions first — they're typically faster. Then move to DI. In DI, check the difficulty of each set before committing — skip heavy sets and return later.

## General English — 40 questions, 40 marks

Reading Comprehension (RC) and grammar-based questions are split roughly 50:50.

**RC (1-2 passages):** The passages in IBPS Clerk Mains are moderate length — 400-600 words. Questions test inference, vocabulary, and main idea. Read the questions before the passage so you know what to look for.

**Grammar and Vocabulary:** Error spotting, cloze test, fill in the blanks, para jumbles. These are faster to attempt than RC.

**Strategy:** Do grammar questions first (faster, clearer). Then attempt RC. This approach protects your time in case RC passages are long.

## Month-by-Month Study Plan (July–December 2026)

**July (Notification Period):** Apply on the first day the form opens. In the meantime, build your foundation — RS Aggarwal for Reasoning and QA, SP Bakshi for English. Start daily current affairs.

**August (Prelims Prep + SBI PO/IBPS PO overlap):** Since IBPS PO Prelims is in August (same study material), your IBPS PO prep directly helps IBPS Clerk Prelims too. Attempt 3-4 Prelims mock tests per week.

**September–early October (Intensive Prelims):** Switch to full mock test mode. Daily Prelims mocks. Identify weak sections. Fix timing issues. Target clearing Prelims comfortably.

**Mid-October (After Prelims — Mains shift):** Dedicate 100% focus to Mains after Prelims. Increase GK study to 45 minutes daily. Attempt weekly Mains mock tests. Practice timed section-wise sets.

**November–December (Mains Final Push):** Full Mains mocks every alternate day. Daily revision of GK notes. Focus on accuracy — every wrong answer costs 0.25 marks. In Mains, accuracy matters more than raw attempt count.

## The One Thing That Will Decide Your Rank

The candidates who clear IBPS Clerk Mains and get their preferred bank allotment are the ones who treat General/Financial Awareness seriously throughout the preparation period. It's the most consistently underestimated section.

Start daily GK from the day you read this. By December 27, 2026, you'll have built 6 months of banking awareness knowledge that most competitors will have scrambled in the last 2 weeks. That 6-month head start shows up directly in your Mains score.

**IBPS Clerk Prelims: October 10–11, 2026 (Confirmed)**
**IBPS Clerk Mains: December 27, 2026 (Confirmed)**
**Apply at: ibps.in** (notification expected July–August 2026)

title: How to Apply for PM Mudra Loan 2026: Step by Step Guide (Shishu
description: PM Mudra Loan 2026: Loans up to ₹20 lakh for small businesses. No collateral. 4 categories explained. Apply online via Udyamimitra or at your nearest bank.
author: Mahitosh Dey
content:
If you run a small business — a tea stall, a tailoring shop, a small dairy, a food cart, a repair garage — and you've needed money to grow but didn't want to deal with banks demanding collateral, the PM Mudra Loan is exactly what the scheme was designed for.

The Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) was launched in 2015 with one goal: give formal credit access to India's micro and small business owners who were previously stuck borrowing from moneylenders at punishing interest rates. In 2026, the scheme has been expanded — the maximum loan amount is now **₹20 lakh**, up from the earlier ₹10 lakh limit.

Here's everything you need to know about PM Mudra Loan 2026 — who qualifies, how much you can get, what documents you need, and how to actually apply.

---

## What Is PM Mudra Loan?

PM Mudra Loan is a **collateral-free business loan** provided by banks, Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), and Microfinance Institutions (MFIs) under the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana. The loans are not given directly by the government — the government guarantees them through MUDRA (Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency Ltd), which means banks can lend without demanding your property as security.

**No collateral.** No guarantor (for most categories). No middleman fee. That's the core promise of the scheme.

---

## The 4 Categories — How Much Can You Get?

PMMY 2026 has four loan categories based on business stage and funding need:

| Category | Loan Amount | Who It's For |
|---|---|---|
| **Shishu** | Up to ₹50,000 | New businesses, first-time entrepreneurs, very small vendors |
| **Kishore** | ₹50,001 to ₹5,00,000 | Existing businesses that need funds to stabilise or expand |
| **Tarun** | ₹5,00,001 to ₹10,00,000 | Established micro-enterprises looking to scale up |
| **Tarun Plus** | ₹10,00,001 to ₹20,00,000 | Businesses that have already repaid a Tarun loan successfully |

**New in 2026 — Tarun Plus:** The government doubled the maximum loan ceiling to ₹20 lakh by introducing the Tarun Plus category. This is specifically for entrepreneurs who have already taken and **fully repaid** a Tarun loan. It bridges the gap between micro-lending and full business loans.

---

## Who Is Eligible?

The scheme is open to:
- Individual entrepreneurs running a small or micro business
- Proprietorships, partnerships, and small enterprises
- Business activities in manufacturing, trading, services, or allied agriculture (food processing, dairy, fishery, poultry, beekeeping, agri-trading)

**Not eligible:**
- Salaried individuals (the loan is for running a business, not personal use)
- Farmers for pure agricultural/crop loans (Kisan Credit Card is the right scheme for that)
- Corporates and large companies

**Who gets priority:**
Women entrepreneurs, SC/ST applicants, and businesses in North-East India often get preferential treatment from lenders — both in processing speed and sometimes in interest rate.

---

## Interest Rates — What to Expect

The government does **not fix** Mudra Loan interest rates. Each lending institution (bank, NBFC, MFI) sets its own rate. These are typical ranges in 2026:

| Category | Typical Interest Rate Range |
|---|---|
| Shishu (up to ₹50,000) | 10% – 12% per annum |
| Kishore (₹50K – ₹5L) | 11% – 15% per annum |
| Tarun (₹5L – ₹10L) | 12% – 16% per annum |
| Tarun Plus (₹10L – ₹20L) | 13% – 16% per annum |

Women entrepreneurs and SC/ST applicants may be offered lower rates under specific bank sub-schemes. Always compare rates from at least 3 lenders before accepting an offer — the Udyamimitra portal (explained below) shows offers from multiple banks side by side.

---

## Documents Required

Keep these ready before you start the application:

**For all categories:**
- Aadhaar card (ID proof)
- PAN card
- Address proof — Aadhaar card, electricity bill, telephone bill (not older than 2 months), or Passport
- Business proof — any one of:
  - Udyam Registration Certificate (MSME registration)
  - GST registration certificate
  - Trade license
  - Shop establishment certificate
- 6 months bank account statements (your business/personal account where transactions happen)
- 2 recent passport-size photographs

**Additionally for Kishore, Tarun, and Tarun Plus:**
- Project report / business plan — how you will use the money and how you will repay
- Income Tax Returns for the last 1–2 years (if filed)
- Balance sheets or profit & loss statement of the business (banks usually ask this for loans above ₹2 lakh)

**For Tarun Plus specifically:**
- Proof that you repaid the previous Tarun loan fully (bank statement or NOC from previous lender)

---

## How to Apply — Step by Step

You have two routes: **online** (faster, compare multiple lenders) or **offline** at a bank branch.

### Online — Via Udyamimitra or JanSamarth Portal (Recommended)

The government has set up two official portals that let you apply to multiple banks at once and receive in-principle approval quickly.

**Udyamimitra:** [udyamimitra.in](https://udyamimitra.in)
**JanSamarth:** [jansamarth.in](https://jansamarth.in)

**Step 1:** Go to udyamimitra.in or jansamarth.in
**Step 2:** Click on "Business Activity Loan" or "PMMY Mudra Loan"
**Step 3:** Register with your mobile number and verify via OTP
**Step 4:** Fill in the application — personal details, business details, loan amount required, and purpose of loan
**Step 5:** The portal will show you in-principle loan offers from multiple banks — compare interest rates and terms
**Step 6:** Accept an offer and the bank will contact you for document verification
**Step 7:** Document verification happens either online or at the bank branch (depends on the lender)
**Step 8:** Loan disbursement to your bank account

Online applications through these portals can get in-principle approvals within minutes. Actual disbursement after document verification typically takes 7–15 working days.

### Offline — At Your Nearest Bank Branch

Go to any of these lenders with your documents:
