No, Agniveers do not receive a pension either during the 4-year service or after exit, because the 4-year term does not qualify for a defined-benefit pension under the current rules. The exit payment is a one-time Seva Nidhi corpus of approximately Rs 11.71 lakh, tax-free under Section 80CCH of the Income Tax Act. Retained Agniveers (25 percent) who continue into regular service accumulate pension eligibility from their retention date onwards, subject to completing the qualifying service period.

**What happens after 4 years of Agniveer service?**
Up to 25 percent of each cohort is retained into regular service based on merit and performance. The remaining 75 percent exit with the Seva Nidhi corpus of approximately Rs 11.71 lakh, a NSQF-mapped skill certificate, and priority in CAPF and state police recruitment through the ex-Agniveer reservation quotas. The first cohort recruited in 2022 exits in October 2026, and approximately 1 lakh Agniveers will complete their term in the last quarter of 2026 under the current 25 percent retention rate.

**Is Agniveer a permanent job?**
No, Agniveer is a fixed 4-year contract, not a permanent post. The Agnipath scheme replaced the older direct recruitment model that offered permanent service until retirement. Only 25 percent of each Agniveer cohort is retained into regular service after the 4-year term, and retention is decided on merit, discipline, and organisational requirements. A proposal to raise retention to 70 to 75 percent for technical trades is under DMA review as of July 2026, but no gazette notification has been issued yet.

**What is the height requirement for Agniveer?**
Height requirements vary by service. Army male candidates typically need 170 cm with regional variations. Navy male candidates need 157 cm. IAF Vayu male candidates need 152.5 cm. Female candidates across all three services need 152 cm minimum. Chest expansion of 5 cm minimum is standard across services. Weight is judged as proportional to height and age at the medical stage rather than fixed to a specific figure.

**How much money does an Agniveer get after 4 years?**
An exiting Agniveer receives approximately Rs 11.71 lakh as the Seva Nidhi corpus, tax-free under Section 80CCH of the Income Tax Act inserted by the Finance Act 2023. The corpus consists of the Agniveer's 30 percent monthly contribution (approximately Rs 5.02 lakh across 48 months), the government's matching contribution (approximately Rs 5.02 lakh), and compound interest at the notified Public Account rate of approximately 7.1 percent per year (approximately Rs 1.67 lakh). The full amount is credited on exit.

**Can an Agniveer apply for CAPF after 4 years?**
Yes, ex-Agniveers can apply for Central Armed Police Forces recruitment with a reserved quota. BSF reserves 50 percent of constable vacancies for ex-Agniveers per the MHA gazette of December 2025, raised from the earlier 10 percent. CRPF, CISF, ITBP, and SSB reserve 10 percent each. Assam Rifles reserves 10 percent. All CAPF recruitments give ex-Agniveers a 3-year age relaxation over the standard age limit for the specific force.

**Is there reservation for Agniveers in state government jobs?**
Yes, several state governments have notified reservation for ex-Agniveers in state police and other posts, with the quantum varying by state. Haryana raised its state police reservation from 10 to 20 percent in April 2026 per the state Cabinet decision. Uttar Pradesh notified a 20 percent horizontal reservation with a 3-year age relaxation for state police. Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Uttarakhand, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Assam, and Rajasthan have all notified reservation in state police, though the specific percentage and cadre coverage vary. Check the specific state gazette for the exact terms.

title: Agniveer Army CEE Result 2026: Check Online, Merit List Guide
description: Complete guide to the Agniveer Army CEE Result 2026 at joinindianarmy.nic.in: result slip, merit list logic, Seva Nidhi and next steps if not qualified.
author: Mahitosh Dey
content:
## How to check Agniveer Army CEE Result 2026

The Agniveer Army CEE (Common Entrance Examination) Result 2026 is published on joinindianarmy.nic.in. Candidates who qualified the Physical Fitness Test and Medical Examination at their regional rally and then sat the online CEE can check their qualifying status using the Roll Number printed on their admit card and their date of birth. This guide covers the exact steps to check the result, how to read the result slip, how the merit list is built, and what happens next for both selected and non-selected candidates.

## Step-by-step: check your CEE result

1. Open the official portal at [joinindianarmy.nic.in](https://joinindianarmy.nic.in).
2. Look for the banner or link titled "Agniveer CEE Result 2026" on the homepage, or navigate to the Recruitment section.
3. Click the result link for your recruitment batch (batch identifier is on your admit card).
4. Enter your Roll Number and Date of Birth (DD/MM/YYYY).
5. Submit and view your result status on screen.
6. Download the PDF result slip and save two copies (one soft, one printout).

Keep your admit card and PFT (Physical Fitness Test) card handy while checking. If the portal is slow near result release, try again after 30 minutes rather than refreshing repeatedly, which sometimes locks the session.

## Understanding your CEE result slip

Your result slip is a single-page PDF that carries the following fields:

- Roll Number and Recruitment Batch ID
- Full Name (as per your Class 10 marksheet)
- Category applied for: GD, Technical, Clerk/SKT, Tradesman (Class 10), or Tradesman (Class 8)
- Marks obtained in the CEE
- Qualifying status: "Qualified", "Not Qualified", or occasionally "Result Awaited"
- Reporting instructions (only if qualified)

The qualifying status alone doesn't guarantee a joining letter. Final selection depends on where your marks place you in the regional merit list for your category. A "Qualified" status means you have cleared the minimum threshold; a joining offer depends on the vacancy count for your Army Recruiting Office (ARO) region and category.

## Recruitment categories covered

Agniveer Army recruitment runs across five main categories. Each has its own eligibility, its own exam structure, and its own regional cutoff.

| Category | Qualification required | Exam duration |
|---|---|---|
| Soldier General Duty (GD) | Class 10, 45% aggregate | 60 minutes |
| Soldier Technical | Class 12 with PCM and English, 50% aggregate | 60 minutes |
| Soldier Clerk / Store Keeper Technical (SKT) | Class 12 (any stream), 60% aggregate, 50% in English and Math | 60 minutes |
| Soldier Tradesman (Class 10) | Class 10, 33% in each subject | 60 minutes |
| Soldier Tradesman (Class 8) | Class 8 pass (for Cook, House Keeper, Mess Keeper, Gardener, Safaiwala) | 60 minutes |

Your result is category-specific. Applying under Technical does not make you eligible for GD merit ranking, even if your marks would qualify under GD.

## How the CEE is scored and how the merit list is built

The CEE is an online, multiple-choice test with a 60-minute time limit. The total marks and section structure vary by category. GD and Technical papers carry 100 marks (50 questions of 2 marks each); the Clerk/SKT paper carries 200 marks across four sections (General Knowledge, General Science, Math, and English). Tradesman-10 carries 100 marks and Tradesman-8 carries 50 marks. Refer to your admit card for the exact split for your paper.

Negative marking applies. Per the Indian Army recruitment notification, wrong answers deduct a proportion of the marks awarded for a correct answer, so blind guessing costs you more than skipping a question you don't know.

The final merit list is not built on CEE marks alone. It is a composite of:

- Marks from the Physical Fitness Test (1.6 km run, pull-ups, 9-feet ditch, zig-zag balance) conducted at the rally
- Marks from the Physical Measurement Test (height, chest, weight)
- Marks obtained in the CEE

The CEE is the largest contributor for GD and Technical, but PFT marks decide the rank order among candidates who tie on CEE. This is why a candidate with slightly lower CEE marks but a top-tier 1.6 km time can outrank one with a higher CEE score but a slower run.

Regional cutoffs are not published centrally. Each ARO releases its own zone-wise merit list based on the number of vacancies notified for that region and the pool of qualified candidates. A qualifying score in one ARO may not translate to a joining letter in another.

### What "Qualified", "Not Qualified" and "Result Awaited" mean

**Qualified**: You have cleared the CEE minimum threshold for your category and are on the regional merit list. A joining letter will follow if your rank falls within the vacancy count for your ARO.

**Not Qualified**: You did not clear the minimum threshold, or your composite score (PFT plus PMT plus CEE) fell below the regional cutoff for your ARO.

**Result Awaited**: Usually a temporary state during answer-key objection windows or when a candidate's PFT or medical documents are still under review. Check again after 48 hours.

## After the result: document verification

Selected candidates receive reporting orders that specify the date and location for document verification (DV). Original documents are checked physically. Missing or mismatched documents lead to disqualification at this stage, even if your CEE rank is good.

Bring originals of the following:

- Class 10 and Class 12 marksheets and passing certificates
- School Leaving Certificate or Transfer Certificate
- Caste certificate (OBC, SC, ST) if applicable, on the prescribed central government format
- Domicile certificate matching the state you applied from
- Character certificate from a gazetted officer or village Sarpanch, dated within the last 6 months
- Recent passport-size colour photographs (usually 20 copies)
- Aadhaar card and PAN card
- Marital status certificate (unmarried certificate) for candidates below 21

Common reasons for rejection at DV: name mismatch across documents, invalid caste certificate format, expired character certificate, or a domicile certificate from a state different from the ARO region.

## Training and the Seva Nidhi package

Candidates who clear DV and final medical are enrolled and sent to the regimental training centre for their arm or service. Training typically lasts 24 to 31 weeks depending on the regiment. Agniveer GD candidates go to the Regimental Training Centres of their respective Infantry regiments; Technical candidates go to arm-specific centres.

Agniveers serve for 4 years. The monthly package, per the Ministry of Defence Agniveer scheme notification of June 2022, is as follows:

| Year | Monthly package | In-hand pay | Contribution to Seva Nidhi (per person) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Year 1 | Rs. 30,000 | Rs. 21,000 | Rs. 9,000 |
| Year 2 | Rs. 33,000 | Rs. 23,100 | Rs. 9,900 |
| Year 3 | Rs. 36,500 | Rs. 25,580 | Rs. 10,950 |
| Year 4 | Rs. 40,000 | Rs. 28,000 | Rs. 12,000 |

The government matches each Agniveer's Seva Nidhi contribution rupee for rupee. The total Seva Nidhi corpus at the end of the 4-year term is approximately Rs. 11.71 lakh, paid tax-free per the scheme notification. 25% of each batch is offered continued regular Army service after the 4-year term, selection based on merit and organisational requirement.

## What to do if you did not qualify

Not clearing the CEE this cycle does not close the door. You can reapply in the next Agniveer recruitment cycle provided you still fall within the 17.5 to 21 age bracket at the time of that new rally. In parallel, other central and state recruitments run on similar timelines and eligibility.

| Alternate path | Eligibility overlap with Agniveer Army | Typical notification window |
|---|---|---|
| Agniveer Navy (SSR, MR) | Class 10 or 12, age 17.5 to 21 | January and July |
| Agniveer Air Force (Vayu) | Class 10 or 12 depending on stream, age 17.5 to 21 | January and June |
| SSC GD Constable (CAPF, NIA, SSF, Assam Rifles) | Class 10, age 18 to 23 | September to November |
| State Police Constable (varies by state) | Class 10 or 12, age varies (usually 18 to 25) | State-notified, rolling |
| CAPF Constable Tradesman (BSF, CRPF, ITBP, CISF, SSB) | Class 10, age 18 to 23 | Yearly, usually first half |

Prepare by studying the areas where you lost marks in the CEE (usually General Knowledge or Mathematics for GD candidates) and by keeping your PFT timing tight. Most alternate paths share the same physical fitness expectations.

## Common portal errors and fixes

- **"Invalid Roll Number"**: Check that you are entering the exact Roll Number from your Admit Card, not your Registration Number or Application ID. These are different numbers.
- **Result link not visible**: The result is released ARO-by-ARO, not centrally. Your ARO's result may not be released on the same day as another ARO's. Check the "Result Notice" section for release dates by region.
- **Portal times out during peak hours**: Traffic spikes in the first hour of release. Try again after 30 to 60 minutes.
- **PDF download fails**: Right-click the download link, choose "Save link as", and save to your device. Some browsers block direct PDF opens.
- **DOB format rejected**: The portal accepts DD/MM/YYYY. Do not use hyphens or type the year first.
- **Result shows "Result Awaited" for several days**: This usually means your PFT or Medical papers are under review. Contact your ARO office directly if the status persists beyond 10 days.

## Frequently asked questions

**How do I check my Agniveer Army CEE Result 2026?**
Go to joinindianarmy.nic.in, click on the result link for your recruitment batch, enter your Roll Number and Date of Birth, and download your PDF result slip. Save two copies.

**What documents do I need to check the result online?**
You need your Roll Number (from your Admit Card) and your Date of Birth. No other documents are needed to view the result. Documents are required only at the physical verification stage after selection.

**My result shows "Not Qualified". Can I reapply?**
Yes. Candidates who don't qualify in one Agniveer Army recruitment cycle can apply in the next cycle, provided they still fall within the 17.5 to 21 age bracket at the time of that rally. Your PFT and medical results from the earlier attempt do not carry over.

**What is the Seva Nidhi amount for Agniveer Army 2026?**
The total Seva Nidhi corpus at the end of 4 years of Agniveer service is approximately Rs. 11.71 lakh, tax-free. It is built from equal contributions by the Agniveer and the government, per the Ministry of Defence Agniveer scheme notification of June 2022.

**Is 25% permanent enrolment confirmed for every batch?**
Yes. The Agniveer scheme specifies that 25% of each batch will be offered the opportunity to continue in regular Army service after 4 years, based on merit and organisational requirement, per the June 2022 scheme announcement.

**Where is the CEE conducted?**
The CEE is conducted online at designated exam centres across India. Your Admit Card, issued about 10 days before the exam, specifies your exam centre, date, and reporting time. The CEE is not conducted at the rally ground.

**How is the merit list built for Agniveer Army selection?**
The final merit list is a composite of your CEE marks, your Physical Fitness Test marks (1.6 km run, pull-ups, 9-feet ditch, zig-zag balance), and your Physical Measurement Test marks (height, chest, weight). Cutoffs are set region-by-region by each Army Recruiting Office based on notified vacancies and the qualified candidate pool.

**Is there negative marking in the Agniveer Army CEE?**
Yes. Per the recruitment notification, wrong answers deduct a proportion of the marks awarded for a correct answer. Blind guessing costs more than skipping a question you don't know.

**Can I check the result offline through my ARO office?**
Yes. If you can't access the portal, visit your Army Recruiting Office in person with your Admit Card. Results are also posted on ARO notice boards. The online portal is the fastest option for candidates outside the ARO city.

**When will the joining letter arrive after "Qualified" status?**
Joining letters typically arrive 6 to 10 weeks after the result, following document verification and final medical clearance. The letter is sent by registered post to the address on your application form.

## Sources

- Indian Army official recruitment portal: [joinindianarmy.nic.in](https://joinindianarmy.nic.in)
- Ministry of Defence Agniveer scheme notification (June 2022): [mod.gov.in](https://mod.gov.in)
- Agniveer scheme details: [agnipathscheme.com](https://agnipathscheme.com)
- Related on this site: [Agniveer 2026 complete guide (Army, Navy, Air Force)](/blog/agniveer-2026-army-navy-air-force-complete-guide) and [SSC GD Constable 2026](/sarkari-naukri/ssc-gd-constable-2026)

title: SSC CGL 2026 salary: post-wise breakdown after 7th Pay Commission
description: Post-wise salary breakdown for SSC CGL 2026 under the 7th Pay Commission. Covers basic pay for all posts from Level 4 to Level 8, current DA rate, HRA by.
author: Mahitosh Dey
content:
## Rs. 25,500 to Rs. 47,600: the range that decides your posting

SSC CGL 2026 fills posts across 5 pay levels under the 7th Pay Commission. The pay level assigned to your post determines your basic pay, and basic pay is the number everything else is calculated from: Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance (TA), NPS contributions, and promotion increments.

This article covers the basic pay for every SSC CGL post, how gross salary is built up from those components, what you actually take home after deductions, and how the salary moves after promotion.

---

## Pay levels under the 7th Pay Commission

The 7th Pay Commission, effective from January 1, 2016, replaced the old pay band and grade pay structure with an 18-level Pay Matrix. Each level has a defined entry basic pay and maximum basic pay. Moving up within a level happens every year through a 3% increment.

SSC CGL posts fall in Levels 4 through 8.

| Pay level | Entry basic pay | Maximum basic pay |
|---|---|---|
| Level 4 | Rs. 25,500 | Rs. 81,100 |
| Level 5 | Rs. 29,200 | Rs. 92,300 |
| Level 6 | Rs. 35,400 | Rs. 1,12,400 |
| Level 7 | Rs. 44,900 | Rs. 1,42,400 |
| Level 8 | Rs. 47,600 | Rs. 1,51,100 |

Source: 7th Central Pay Commission Pay Matrix, Ministry of Finance notification dated July 25, 2016.

---

## Post-wise pay level

| Post | Department | Pay level | Entry basic pay |
|---|---|---|---|
| Assistant Audit Officer (AAO) | C&AG | Level 8 | Rs. 47,600 |
| Assistant Accounts Officer | C&AG | Level 8 | Rs. 47,600 |
| Inspector of Income Tax | CBDT | Level 7 | Rs. 44,900 |
| Inspector (Central Excise/CGST) | CBIC | Level 7 | Rs. 44,900 |
| Inspector (Preventive Officer) | CBIC | Level 7 | Rs. 44,900 |
| Inspector (Examiner) | CBIC | Level 7 | Rs. 44,900 |
| Assistant Enforcement Officer | Enforcement Directorate | Level 7 | Rs. 44,900 |
| Inspector of Posts | Department of Posts | Level 7 | Rs. 44,900 |
| Sub Inspector | CBI | Level 6 | Rs. 35,400 |
| Sub Inspector | NIA | Level 6 | Rs. 35,400 |
| Junior Statistical Officer | Ministry of Statistics | Level 6 | Rs. 35,400 |
| Statistical Investigator Grade II | Registrar General of India | Level 6 | Rs. 35,400 |
| Divisional Accountant | C&AG | Level 6 | Rs. 35,400 |
| Auditor | C&AG | Level 5 | Rs. 29,200 |
| Auditor | CGDA | Level 5 | Rs. 29,200 |
| Auditor | Other ministries | Level 5 | Rs. 29,200 |
| Accountant / Junior Accountant | Various | Level 5 | Rs. 29,200 |
| Senior Secretariat Assistant (UDC) | CSS / various | Level 4 | Rs. 25,500 |
| Tax Assistant | CBDT / CBIC | Level 4 | Rs. 25,500 |

Source: SSC CGL 2024 official notification, Staff Selection Commission.

---

## How gross salary is calculated

Gross salary has four components: basic pay, DA, HRA, and TA.

### Dearness Allowance (DA)

The Cabinet revises DA twice a year, in January and July, based on the All India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (AICPI-IW). As of January 1, 2025, DA stands at 55% of basic pay, per the Cabinet Secretariat revision dated March 2025.

For an Inspector of Income Tax with basic pay Rs. 44,900:
DA = 55% x Rs. 44,900 = Rs. 24,695/month.

### House Rent Allowance (HRA)

HRA depends on the city where you're posted. When DA crossed 50%, HRA moved to the enhanced slab, per Finance Ministry Office Memorandum No. F.2(2)/2017-E.II(B).

| City category | HRA (DA above 50%) | Cities included |
|---|---|---|
| X | 27% of basic pay | Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad |
| Y | 18% of basic pay | State capitals and cities with 5 lakh+ population |
| Z | 9% of basic pay | All other places |

### Transport Allowance (TA)

TA is a fixed monthly amount plus DA on that amount. For Level 3 to 8 employees in X cities (per MoF OM F.No. 21011/01/2017-Estt.(AL)):

- X cities: Rs. 3,600/month + DA on TA
- Other cities: Rs. 1,800/month + DA on TA

At 55% DA, TA for Level 3-8 in an X city: Rs. 3,600 + (55% x Rs. 3,600) = Rs. 5,580/month.
For other cities: Rs. 1,800 + (55% x Rs. 1,800) = Rs. 2,790/month.

---

## Gross salary worked example: Inspector of Income Tax in Delhi

| Component | Calculation | Monthly amount |
|---|---|---|
| Basic pay | Fixed at entry | Rs. 44,900 |
| DA (55%) | 55% x 44,900 | Rs. 24,695 |
| HRA (27%, X city) | 27% x 44,900 | Rs. 12,123 |
| TA (X city, 55% DA) | 3,600 + 1,980 | Rs. 5,580 |
| Gross | Sum | Rs. 87,298 |

---

## Gross salary by post (Delhi, 55% DA)

| Post | Basic pay | DA (55%) | HRA (27%) | TA | Gross |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AAO / Asst. Accounts Officer | Rs. 47,600 | Rs. 26,180 | Rs. 12,852 | Rs. 5,580 | Rs. 92,212 |
| Inspector IT / CGST / AEO / Posts | Rs. 44,900 | Rs. 24,695 | Rs. 12,123 | Rs. 5,580 | Rs. 87,298 |
| SI CBI / NIA, JSO, Div. Accountant | Rs. 35,400 | Rs. 19,470 | Rs. 9,558 | Rs. 5,580 | Rs. 70,008 |
| Auditor / Accountant | Rs. 29,200 | Rs. 16,060 | Rs. 7,884 | Rs. 5,580 | Rs. 58,724 |
| Tax Assistant / UDC | Rs. 25,500 | Rs. 14,025 | Rs. 6,885 | Rs. 5,580 | Rs. 51,990 |

---

## How city affects salary

The difference between a Delhi posting and a small-town posting comes entirely from HRA and TA. Basic pay and DA are the same everywhere.

| City category | Inspector IT gross | Compared to Delhi |
|---|---|---|
| Delhi (X) | Rs. 87,298 | Baseline |
| Lucknow (Y) | Rs. 80,467 | Rs. 6,831 less |
| Small town (Z) | Rs. 76,426 | Rs. 10,872 less |

For the Y-city calculation: HRA = 18% x Rs. 44,900 = Rs. 8,082; TA = Rs. 2,790. For Z city: HRA = 9% x Rs. 44,900 = Rs. 4,041; TA = Rs. 2,790.

---

## Deductions

### NPS (National Pension System)

All central government employees recruited after January 1, 2004, are covered under NPS. The employee contributes 10% of (basic pay + DA), and the government contributes 14% on the same base.

| Post | Basic + DA | NPS deduction (10%) |
|---|---|---|
| AAO | Rs. 73,780 | Rs. 7,378 |
| Inspector IT / CGST | Rs. 69,595 | Rs. 6,960 |
| SI CBI / JSO | Rs. 54,870 | Rs. 5,487 |
| Auditor | Rs. 45,260 | Rs. 4,526 |
| Tax Assistant / UDC | Rs. 39,525 | Rs. 3,953 |

### Income tax

Under the new tax regime for FY 2025-26, the Section 87A rebate covers the full tax liability for taxable income up to Rs. 12,00,000 (after the Rs. 75,000 standard deduction). Inspector IT in Delhi earns a gross of approximately Rs. 10.48 lakh annually. After the standard deduction, net taxable income is Rs. 9.73 lakh. This falls under the Rs. 12 lakh rebate threshold, so income tax is nil under the new regime.

Inspector-level employees who opt for the old regime and claim 80C (Rs. 1.5 lakh), 80CCD(1B) (Rs. 50,000), and standard deduction (Rs. 50,000) will have taxable income around Rs. 8.5 lakh. Tax works out to roughly Rs. 70,000-75,000 per year, or Rs. 5,800-6,200/month.

The right regime depends on your deductions. If you have a home loan, the old regime may lower your tax bill more.

### CGHS contribution

Employees in CGHS-covered cities contribute Rs. 250 to Rs. 1,000/month depending on pay level, for health cover that extends to spouse, dependent children, and dependent parents.

---

## Approximate in-hand salary (Delhi, entry pay, 55% DA, new regime)

| Post | Gross | NPS | CGHS | Approx. in-hand |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AAO / Asst. Accounts Officer | Rs. 92,212 | Rs. 7,378 | Rs. 700 | Rs. 83,000-85,000 |
| Inspector IT / CGST / AEO | Rs. 87,298 | Rs. 6,960 | Rs. 500 | Rs. 79,000-80,000 |
| SI CBI / NIA / JSO | Rs. 70,008 | Rs. 5,487 | Rs. 350 | Rs. 63,000-65,000 |
| Auditor / Accountant | Rs. 58,724 | Rs. 4,526 | Rs. 250 | Rs. 53,000-54,000 |
| Tax Assistant / UDC | Rs. 51,990 | Rs. 3,953 | Rs. 250 | Rs. 47,000-48,000 |

Income tax is excluded from the above table. It varies by regime and individual deductions.

---

## Allowances specific to certain posts

Not every SSC CGL post carries the same set of allowances.

Inspectors in CGST and Customs receive a uniform allowance of Rs. 10,000 per year, per MoF OM dated 2017. Sub Inspectors in CBI receive a risk allowance of Rs. 300 per month. Employees posted to northeastern states receive a Special Duty Allowance of 25% of basic pay, per DOPT guidelines. Children Education Allowance is Rs. 2,250 per child per month (maximum 2 children), with a separate hostel subsidy of Rs. 6,750 per child per month if the child stays in a hostel away from the parent's place of posting.

---

## Salary after promotion

Promotion in central government service follows the Departmental Promotion Committee (DPC) cycle and is tied to vacancy availability in the higher grade.

For Inspector of Income Tax (Level 7):
Promotion to Income Tax Officer (ITO) moves the pay to Level 8 (Rs. 47,600 basic). This typically happens within 3 to 5 years, subject to passing the internal exam and vacancy clearance. ITO further promotes to Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax (Level 10, Rs. 56,100 basic) after another 3 to 5 years. From there, the path leads to Deputy Commissioner (Level 11), Joint Commissioner (Level 12), and Commissioner (Level 13), all within the Group A gazetted cadre.

For AAO (Level 8):
The path goes to Senior Audit Officer (Level 10, Rs. 56,100), then Audit Officer (Level 11, Rs. 67,700), Deputy Accountant General, and eventually Principal Accountant General.

For Tax Assistant (Level 4):
Promotion to Senior Tax Assistant and then to Examiner or Inspector requires clearing a departmental examination. The entire path from Level 4 to Level 7 typically takes 10 to 15 years.

---

## Other benefits

Central government employees get several benefits that don't show up in the monthly salary slip.

Leave Travel Concession (LTC) covers travel to the hometown once every 2 years and travel anywhere in India once every 4 years. The reimbursement covers rail or air fares (as permitted by the entitlement class) for the employee and family.

Government accommodation is available on a waiting list basis. In smaller cities, the wait is typically 1 to 3 years. In Delhi, the wait for Type III and Type IV quarters can run to 6 to 10 years depending on seniority.

The NPS government contribution of 14% on (basic + DA) builds a separate retirement corpus alongside the employee's own 10% contribution. For an Inspector IT at entry level, the government deposits Rs. 9,743/month into the NPS account (14% of Rs. 69,595), entirely separate from the salary.

---

## Which SSC CGL post pays the most

At entry, AAO and Assistant Accounts Officer under C&AG (Level 8, Rs. 47,600 basic) carry the highest basic pay. In Delhi, gross is approximately Rs. 92,212/month and in-hand is approximately Rs. 83,000-85,000/month.

Among Level 7 posts, gross salary is the same for all 6 posts (Inspector IT, Inspector CGST, Preventive Officer, Examiner, AEO, Inspector Posts). The difference in total monthly compensation between these posts comes from specific allowances: Inspectors in CGST and Customs get a uniform allowance, SI CBI gets a risk allowance, and AEO in ED may get postings with additional operational allowances.

Junior Statistical Officer (Level 6) and SI in NIA (Level 6) both have the same basic pay. JSO has a relatively faster promotion track in the Ministry of Statistics cadre compared to the general audit cadre.

---

## Frequently asked questions
**What is the in-hand salary for SSC CGL Inspector of Income Tax in 2025?**
For an Inspector of Income Tax posted in Delhi at entry Level 7, gross salary is Rs. 87,298/month at 55% DA (as of January 2025, per Cabinet Secretariat revision dated March 2025). After NPS deduction of Rs. 6,960 and CGHS contribution, in-hand salary under the new tax regime is approximately Rs. 79,000 to Rs. 80,000/month.

**What is the SSC CGL AAO salary in 2025?**
The Assistant Audit Officer carries Pay Level 8 with entry basic pay of Rs. 47,600. In Delhi at 55% DA, gross monthly salary is Rs. 92,212. In-hand, after NPS deduction of Rs. 7,378, is approximately Rs. 83,000 to Rs. 85,000/month.

**What is the current DA rate for SSC CGL employees?**
The Dearness Allowance for all central government employees, including SSC CGL post holders, is 55% of basic pay as of January 1, 2025, per the Cabinet Secretariat revision dated March 2025. DA is revised in January and July each year based on the AICPI-IW index.

**What is the HRA for SSC CGL employees posted in Delhi?**
SSC CGL employees posted in Delhi receive HRA at 27% of basic pay. This enhanced rate applies because DA has exceeded 50%, per Finance Ministry OM No. F.2(2)/2017-E.II(B). For an Inspector IT with basic pay Rs. 44,900, HRA in Delhi works out to Rs. 12,123/month.

**What is the SSC CGL Tax Assistant in-hand salary?**
Tax Assistants in CBDT and CBIC are in Pay Level 4 with entry basic pay of Rs. 25,500. In Delhi at 55% DA, gross is Rs. 51,990/month. After NPS deduction of Rs. 3,953, in-hand is approximately Rs. 47,000 to Rs. 48,000/month.

**Do SSC CGL employees get the old pension scheme?**
SSC CGL recruits after January 1, 2004, are under the National Pension System (NPS), not the Old Pension Scheme (OPS). Under NPS, the employee contributes 10% and the government contributes 14% of (basic pay + DA) each month. The accumulated corpus is converted to an annuity at retirement.

**How much does salary increase after promotion in SSC CGL?**
An Inspector of Income Tax (Level 7, Rs. 44,900 basic) promoted to Income Tax Officer moves to Level 8 (Rs. 47,600 basic): a jump of Rs. 2,700 in basic pay, which at 55% DA adds approximately Rs. 4,185 to gross monthly salary. The larger salary jump comes with promotion to Assistant Commissioner (Level 10, Rs. 56,100 basic), which adds roughly Rs. 11,200 to basic pay and approximately Rs. 17,360 to gross.

---

## Quick reference: SSC CGL 2026 salary summary

| Post | Level | Basic pay | Gross in Delhi | Approx. in-hand |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AAO / Asst. Accounts Officer | 8 | Rs. 47,600 | Rs. 92,212 | Rs. 83,000-85,000 |
| Inspector IT / CGST / AEO / Posts | 7 | Rs. 44,900 | Rs. 87,298 | Rs. 79,000-80,000 |
| SI CBI/NIA, JSO, Div. Accountant | 6 | Rs. 35,400 | Rs. 70,008 | Rs. 63,000-65,000 |
| Auditor / Accountant | 5 | Rs. 29,200 | Rs. 58,724 | Rs. 53,000-54,000 |
| Tax Assistant / UDC | 4 | Rs. 25,500 | Rs. 51,990 | Rs. 47,000-48,000 |

All gross figures assume Delhi (X city) posting at 55% DA (January 2025 rate). In-hand figures assume the new tax regime for FY 2025-26 and exclude income tax, which depends on the regime chosen and deductions claimed.

9 of the 19 SSC CGL posts fall in Level 7 or Level 8. Every one of them clears Rs. 80,000/month gross in Delhi at current DA rates, and the promotion path from Level 7 leads to Group A gazetted service within 8 to 12 years. That's the number most candidates are actually comparing when they choose between SSC CGL and a private sector offer.

title: WB Gram Panchayat 2026: Complete Guide to 11,000 Posts
description: Complete guide to WB Gram Panchayat Recruitment 2026: post-wise eligibility, selection process, salary breakdown, and how to apply at wbprms.in portal.
author: SarkariDarapan
content:
## 11,000 government jobs in West Bengal's Gram Panchayats, and registration is already open

West Bengal opened registration for the Gram Panchayat Recruitment 2026 on June 10, 2026 at wbprms.in. The state government originally approved 6,500 posts. That count was then raised to 11,000+ to clear the backlog of vacancies across Gram Panchayats in all districts.

If you're in West Bengal and looking for a government job, this is one of the largest state recruitment drives this year.

---

## What posts are on offer

Five post types are included in this recruitment. The qualification requirements go from Class 8 to a graduate degree, which means people at very different education levels can apply.

| Post | Minimum qualification | Computer required |
|---|---|---|
| Executive Assistant | Graduation from a recognized university | Yes |
| Data Entry Operator (DEO) | Class 12 pass | Yes (certificate or diploma) |
| Nirman Sahayak | Class 10 pass | No |
| Gram Panchayat Karmee | Class 8 pass | No |
| Clerk | Class 12 pass | No |

The DEO and Executive Assistant posts specifically require a computer certificate or diploma from a recognized institution. If you're applying for those, make sure your certificate is from an institution the state government recognizes.

---

## Who can apply

The state government raised the upper age limit for Group C and Group D posts to 45 years. All Gram Panchayat posts fall in that classification, so the 45-year ceiling applies here.

Age relaxation for SC/ST and OBC candidates follows standard West Bengal state government rules.

There's one non-negotiable language requirement: you need to be able to read, write, and speak Bengali. Candidates from the hill subdivisions (Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Kurseong) can apply with Nepali proficiency instead of Bengali. Everyone else needs Bengali.

---

## How to apply at wbprms.in

The official portal for this recruitment is wbprms.in. The West Bengal Panchayat Recruitment Management System handles everything: registration, application, fee payment, and eventually admit cards and results.

Here's what the registration process looks like:

1. Go to wbprms.in and open the WB Gram Panchayat Recruitment 2026 section.
2. Register with your email ID and mobile number. You'll get your login credentials on that number.
3. Log in and fill in the application form. You'll need your personal details, educational qualifications, district preference, and category information.
4. Upload a recent photo and signature in the format the portal specifies.
5. Pay the application fee if it applies to you. SC/ST/OBC/PwD candidates are expected to be exempt, though the official fee structure hasn't been confirmed yet.
6. Submit and save the confirmation number.

The last date to apply hasn't been announced. Keep checking wbprms.in or follow our [Telegram channel](https://t.me/sarkaridarapaninfo) for the update.

---

## What the written test looks like

The written examination is managed by the District Level Selection Committee (DLSC). It's objective MCQ, 85 marks total.

Four subjects are tested: English, Bengali, Arithmetic, and General Knowledge. The GK section has a specific rural development angle, which makes sense given the role. Questions tend to cover Panchayati Raj, rural schemes, and WB state governance rather than just standard current affairs.

Candidates who clear the written test go to an interview, and then document verification.

There's no detailed syllabus document released yet. In past WB Panchayat recruitments, the arithmetic section covered Class 8 to Class 10 level maths. The GK section covered state government schemes, Panchayati Raj Act provisions, and basic rural administration. That's a reasonable starting point for preparation.

---

## Salary you can expect

Pay is under the West Bengal State Pay Matrix. The exact pay matrix levels for each post will be in the official notification.

For reference: the maximum basic pay for higher-grade posts goes up to Rs. 92,100 per month, per WB state pay norms. In practice, entry-level posts like GP Karmee will be placed at a lower level with a corresponding lower starting basic pay. Add state DA, HRA, and other admissible allowances on top.

This is a permanent state government job with job security, pension under NPS, and annual increments.

---

## Why this recruitment matters for WB job seekers

11,000 vacancies in a single drive is unusual. The state has had a large backlog of unfilled Gram Panchayat posts for several years, partly due to legal challenges and delayed schedules. This recruitment is an attempt to fill that backlog in one go.

The posts are spread across all districts, which means most candidates can find something close to home. Executive Assistant and DEO roles require graduation or Class 12 with computer skills. But GP Karmee requires only a Class 8 pass, which opens this up to a much wider pool than most government jobs.

If you're in that category, don't sleep on the last date announcement. These drives can close quickly once a date is set.

---

## Frequently asked questions

**How many vacancies are there in WB Gram Panchayat Recruitment 2026?**
11,000+ vacancies across posts including Executive Assistant, DEO, Nirman Sahayak, GP Karmee, and Clerk. The original sanction was 6,500, increased by 4,500 additional posts, per state government orders.

**Where do I apply for WB Gram Panchayat Recruitment 2026?**
All applications go through the official portal at wbprms.in. There is no offline or postal application route.

**What is the age limit for WB Gram Panchayat Recruitment 2026?**
The upper age limit is 45 years for all posts. Standard age relaxation applies for SC/ST and OBC candidates under WB state government rules.

**Is Bengali language compulsory for these posts?**
Yes. Bengali proficiency (reading, writing, speaking) is a mandatory requirement for all posts. Candidates from Darjeeling, Kalimpong, and Kurseong subdivisions can apply with Nepali instead.

**What is the minimum qualification for Gram Panchayat Karmee?**
Class 8 pass from a recognized school. This is the lowest qualification requirement among all posts in this recruitment.

**When is the last date to apply?**
The last date has not been announced as of June 2026. Check wbprms.in for the official update.

---

## Sources

- Official portal: [wbprms.in](https://wbprms.in)
- Karmasandhan report on 11,000 vacancy increase: [karmasandhan.com](https://www.karmasandhan.com/wb-gram-panchayat-recruitment-2026/)

title: SSC CHSL 2026 admit card: how to download your hall ticket from
description: Download SSC CHSL Tier 1 2026 admit card from ssc.gov.in using your Registration ID and date of birth. Steps to download, what to carry to the exam centre.
author: Mahitosh Dey
content:
---

SSC releases the CHSL Tier 1 admit card approximately 7 to 10 days before the exam date on ssc.gov.in. The admit card is mandatory to enter the examination hall — no candidate is allowed in without it.

This guide covers how to download the admit card, what it contains, what to bring on exam day, and what to do if there's an error.

## How to download SSC CHSL 2026 admit card

1. Go to the official SSC website: [ssc.gov.in](https://ssc.gov.in)
2. Click on "Admit Card" in the top navigation or on the homepage banner.
3. Select "CHSL" from the list of exams.
4. You'll be redirected to your regional SSC website (NR, SR, ER, WR, CR, MPR, KKR, NER, NWR based on your application region).
5. Enter your Registration ID (from your CHSL 2026 application) and either your Date of Birth or Password.
6. Click Submit.
7. Your admit card will appear on screen. Download and save it as a PDF.
8. Print on A4 paper. Don't resize or compress the print — it may affect the barcode and photograph.

SSC also sends admit card links to your registered email and mobile number via SMS. Check both if you're having trouble finding the link on the website.

## What the SSC CHSL 2026 admit card shows

| Field | What to check |
|---|---|
| Candidate name | Matches your application exactly |
| Roll number | Note this — you'll need it to check results later |
| Registration number | Same as your application registration ID |
| Photograph | Clear, matches your uploaded photo |
| Signature | Visible and matches your registration |
| Exam date and shift | Morning (10:00 AM) or Afternoon (3:00 PM) — check carefully |
| Exam centre name and address | Locate the centre on Google Maps before exam day |
| Reporting time | Usually 30 to 60 minutes before the exam starts |

If any field — especially your name, date of birth, or photograph — is wrong, contact SSC through the official helpdesk at ssc.gov.in immediately. SSC does not allow corrections on exam day.

## SSC CHSL Tier 1 2026 exam pattern

The Tier 1 exam is computer-based. 60 minutes to answer 100 questions.

| Section | Questions | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| English Language and Comprehension | 25 | 50 |
| General Intelligence | 25 | 50 |
| Quantitative Aptitude (Basic Arithmetic) | 25 | 50 |
| General Awareness | 25 | 50 |
| Total | 100 | 200 |

Each correct answer: 2 marks. Each wrong answer: 0.50 marks deducted. Unattempted questions carry no penalty.

VH candidates and candidates with cerebral palsy get 80 minutes. OH candidates who cannot use a keyboard get a scribe and 80 minutes.

## What to carry to the exam centre

You must bring both of these on exam day:

1. **Printed admit card** — colour printout preferred; clear photograph and barcode must be visible.
2. **Original photo ID** — one of: Aadhaar card, PAN card, Voter ID, Passport, Driving License, Employee ID (for Central/State government employees).

The photo ID you bring must be the same one you mentioned during registration, though SSC generally accepts any valid government-issued photo ID at the centre.

Don't bring: mobile phones, smart watches, calculators, earphones, or any electronic device. They're not allowed inside the exam hall and may result in disqualification. Bags and water bottles are also generally not permitted — check the exam centre instructions on the back of your admit card.

## If your admit card has an error

Contact SSC immediately through the regional helpdesk listed on ssc.gov.in. Don't wait until exam day.

For name or date of birth corrections, SSC may ask you to bring supporting documents to the exam centre. Carry your original Class 10 marksheet or certificate on exam day regardless — it serves as proof of name, date of birth, and qualification.

If the photograph on the admit card is blurry or absent, carry extra passport-size photographs matching your registration photo. Most exam centres ask for one photograph to paste on the attendance sheet.

## FAQ

#### Where do I download the SSC CHSL 2026 admit card?

At ssc.gov.in, under the Admit Card section. You'll be redirected to your regional SSC website. Use your Registration ID and date of birth or password to log in and download it.

#### What if I forget my Registration ID for SSC CHSL 2026?

Log in to your SSC One account at ssc.gov.in using your registered mobile number or email. Your registration ID is visible in the dashboard under "Applied Applications." If you can't access your account, use the "Forgot Password" option on the login page.

#### Can I take a screenshot of the admit card on my phone instead of printing it?

No. SSC requires a physical printout of the admit card. A digital copy on your phone won't be accepted at the exam centre.

#### Is the SSC CHSL admit card released separately for Tier 1 and Tier 2?

Yes. The Tier 1 admit card and Tier 2 admit card are released separately, usually 7 to 10 days before each respective exam. The guide above covers Tier 1. Tier 2 admit cards follow the same download process.

#### Can I appear in SSC CHSL Tier 1 2026 without an admit card?

No. The admit card is compulsory. Candidates without a printed admit card are not allowed to enter the examination hall, regardless of other documents they carry.

#### What happens if my name on the admit card doesn't match my ID?

Report the discrepancy to SSC through the regional helpdesk immediately. On exam day, carry original supporting documents (Class 10 marksheet showing correct name) and inform the invigilator. Don't attempt to alter the admit card in any way.

## Sources

- SSC official website: [ssc.gov.in](https://ssc.gov.in)
- SSC One candidate portal: [ssc.gov.in/candidate-login](https://ssc.gov.in/candidate-login)
- SSC CHSL 2025 notification (for exam pattern reference): [ssc.gov.in/notice](https://ssc.gov.in/notice)
- Regional SSC websites: sscnr.net.in (Northern), sscswr.org (Southern Western), rrbcdg.gov.in

title: SSC CGL Syllabus 2026 - Complete Topic-Wise Breakdown for Tier 1
description: Detailed SSC CGL 2026 syllabus covering every topic for Tier 1 and Tier 2 with weightage, important chapters, and preparation priority for each subject.
author: Mahitosh Dey
content:
## What Does the SSC CGL 2026 Syllabus Cover?

The SSC CGL (Staff Selection Commission Combined Graduate Level) exam syllabus can feel overwhelming when you first look at it. There are multiple subjects, two tiers, and hundreds of topics. But here is the truth — if you understand the syllabus properly and know which topics matter the most, you can prepare smartly instead of working hard on everything.

I went through this exact confusion when I started my SSC CGL preparation. I wasted the first month studying topics that barely had any questions in the exam. Once I understood the actual topic-wise breakdown and weightage, my preparation became much more focused and productive.

This guide gives you the **complete topic-wise syllabus** for both Tier 1 and Tier 2, along with the expected number of questions from each topic and which ones to prioritise. For the full exam notification, visit our [SSC CGL 2026 page](/sarkari-naukri/ssc-cgl-2026) and stay updated with all [SSC updates](/category/ssc).

## SSC CGL 2026 Exam Pattern at a Glance

Before diving into the syllabus, let us understand the exam structure:

| Feature | Tier 1 | Tier 2 |
|---------|--------|--------|
| Mode | Computer Based (Online) | Computer Based (Online) |
| Total Questions | 100 | Varies by paper |
| Total Marks | 200 | 390 (Paper 1 compulsory) |
| Duration | 60 minutes | 2 hours 15 minutes (Paper 1) |
| Negative Marking | 0.50 per wrong answer | 1.0 or 0.25 per wrong answer |
| Purpose | Screening round | Final selection |

Tier 1 is the qualifying round — you need to clear the cutoff to sit for Tier 2. Your final merit is based mostly on Tier 2 marks, so both tiers are important but Tier 2 carries more weight in your selection.

## Tier 1 Syllabus - Topic-Wise Breakdown

Tier 1 has four sections with 25 questions each. Here is the detailed topic-wise breakdown for every section.

### General Intelligence and Reasoning (25 Questions, 50 Marks)

Reasoning is usually the highest-scoring section for well-prepared candidates. Most questions are logic-based and do not require memorisation.

**High Priority Topics** (expect 15-18 questions from these):
- **Analogy** — 3 to 4 questions. You get a pair and need to find a similar relationship
- **Classification / Odd One Out** — 2 to 3 questions. Identify the item that does not belong
- **Coding-Decoding** — 2 to 3 questions. Letter and number-based coding patterns
- **Series** — 2 to 3 questions. Number series, letter series, and figure series
- **Blood Relations** — 1 to 2 questions. Family tree-based problems
- **Direction Sense** — 1 to 2 questions. Map and compass-based questions
- **Syllogism** — 1 to 2 questions. Statement and conclusion problems

**Medium Priority Topics** (expect 5-8 questions):
- Mirror and Water Images
- Paper Folding and Cutting
- Embedded Figures
- Figure Counting (triangles, squares)
- Pattern Completion
- Matrix and Dice problems

**Study tip**: Practice 20-30 reasoning questions daily. This section improves dramatically with regular practice.

### General Awareness (25 Questions, 50 Marks)

This section tests your knowledge of current events and static general knowledge. Many candidates struggle here because the syllabus feels unlimited.

**High Priority Topics** (expect 15-17 questions):
- **Indian History** — 3 to 4 questions on Ancient, Medieval, and Modern India
- **Indian Polity** — 3 to 4 questions on Constitution, Parliament, Fundamental Rights
- **Geography** — 2 to 3 questions on Indian and World Geography
- **General Science** — 3 to 4 questions on Physics, Chemistry, Biology basics
- **Current Affairs** — 3 to 4 questions from the last 6-8 months

**Medium Priority Topics** (expect 6-8 questions):
- Indian Economy (GDP, budget, banking terms)
- Awards and Honours
- Books and Authors
- Sports events
- Government Schemes
- International organisations
- Important dates and events

**Study tip**: Read Lucent's General Knowledge for static GK and follow a monthly current affairs PDF for the last 6 months.

### Quantitative Aptitude (25 Questions, 50 Marks)

This section carries the most weight in preparation time because the topics are vast and require regular practice.

**High Priority Topics** (expect 16-18 questions):
- **Percentage** — 2 to 3 questions. Foundation for Profit/Loss and SI/CI
- **Profit and Loss** — 1 to 2 questions
- **Simple and Compound Interest** — 1 to 2 questions
- **Ratio and Proportion** — 1 to 2 questions
- **Average** — 1 to 2 questions
- **Time and Work** — 1 to 2 questions including pipe and cistern problems
- **Time, Speed, and Distance** — 1 to 2 questions including trains and boats
- **Data Interpretation** — 3 to 4 questions based on tables, pie charts, or bar graphs
- **Geometry** — 2 to 3 questions on triangles, circles, and quadrilaterals
- **Algebra** — 1 to 2 questions on simplification and equations

**Medium Priority Topics** (expect 5-7 questions):
- Trigonometry (heights and distances, identities)
- Mensuration (area and volume formulas)
- Number System
- Mixture and Alligation
- Surds and Indices

**Study tip**: Master arithmetic first (Percentage through Speed-Distance). These topics form a chain — once you understand Percentage, Profit/Loss becomes easy, and so on.

### English Comprehension (25 Questions, 50 Marks)

English tests your grammar, vocabulary, and reading ability. If English is not your strong point, focus on the high-scoring topics.

**High Priority Topics** (expect 15-18 questions):
- **Error Spotting** — 3 to 4 questions. Find grammatical errors in sentences
- **Cloze Test** — 4 to 5 questions. Fill in blanks in a passage
- **Reading Comprehension** — 4 to 5 questions based on a passage
- **Sentence Improvement** — 2 to 3 questions
- **Synonyms and Antonyms** — 2 to 3 questions

**Medium Priority Topics** (expect 5-8 questions):
- Idioms and Phrases
- One Word Substitution
- Active/Passive Voice
- Direct/Indirect Speech
- Spelling Correction
- Para Jumbles

**Study tip**: Read English newspapers daily for 30 minutes. It improves comprehension, vocabulary, and grammar all at once.

## Tier 2 Syllabus

Tier 2 Paper 1 is compulsory for all candidates and is divided into modules:

### Module 1: Mathematical Abilities (30 questions, 90 marks)

Covers the same topics as Tier 1 Quantitative Aptitude but at a **higher difficulty level**. Expect more advanced questions on Algebra, Geometry, Trigonometry, and Data Interpretation. You need to solve problems faster here since the question count is higher relative to time.

### Module 2: Reasoning and General Intelligence (30 questions, 90 marks)

Similar topics as Tier 1 but with more complex patterns, advanced coding-decoding, and multi-step logical reasoning. Matrix and arrangement-based questions are more frequent here.

### Module 3: English Language and Comprehension (45 questions, 90 marks)

Includes everything from Tier 1 plus **essay writing** (250 words) and **letter writing** (150 words). This is a significant addition. Practice writing essays on current topics and both formal and informal letters.

### Module 4: General Awareness (25 questions, 50 marks)

Same topics as Tier 1 but with more specific and detailed questions. The current affairs component is more recent — focus on the last 3 months especially.

### Module 5: Computer Knowledge (20 questions, 40 marks)

- Computer fundamentals (hardware, software, memory)
- Operating Systems basics
- MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
- Internet and Networking basics
- Database basics (DBMS concepts)
- Computer security (virus, firewall, encryption)

### Special Papers

- **Paper 2 — Statistics** (for Junior Statistical Officer): Covers collection, classification, and presentation of data, measures of central tendency and dispersion, probability, sampling, and statistical inference
- **Paper 3 — General Studies (Finance and Economics)** (for Assistant Audit Officer and Assistant Accounts Officer): Covers financial accounting, economics, and governance

## How to Prioritise Your Study

With such a vast syllabus, you need a clear priority system. Here is what I recommend based on the exam pattern and previous years' analysis:

| Priority | Topics | Why |
|----------|--------|-----|
| First | Arithmetic (Percentage to Speed-Distance), Reasoning basics, Error Spotting | These topics appear in every exam and are easy to master |
| Second | Geometry, Trigonometry, DI, Reading Comprehension | Higher marks but need more time to prepare |
| Third | Static GK, Computer Knowledge | Requires memorisation — start early and revise often |
| Fourth | Current Affairs, Essay Writing | Do these alongside your main preparation daily |

**My recommended daily schedule**:
- 2 hours on Quantitative Aptitude
- 1.5 hours on Reasoning
- 1 hour on English
- 1 hour on General Awareness
- 30 minutes on Current Affairs
- 1 mock test (alternate days)

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is the Tier 1 and Tier 2 syllabus the same for SSC CGL 2026?

No, the syllabus is not the same. Tier 1 covers four subjects — Reasoning, General Awareness, Quantitative Aptitude, and English. Tier 2 includes all four plus additional modules like Computer Knowledge, Data Entry, and for some posts Statistics or General Studies (Finance and Economics). The difficulty level in Tier 2 is also higher than Tier 1.

### Which topics have the highest weightage in SSC CGL Tier 1?

In Reasoning, Analogy, Classification, and Coding-Decoding carry the highest weightage. In Quantitative Aptitude, Arithmetic topics like Percentage, Profit and Loss, Time and Work, and Data Interpretation are most important. In English, Error Spotting, Cloze Test, and Reading Comprehension dominate. In General Awareness, Static GK (History, Polity, Geography) and Science carry the most marks.

### Do I need to study the same material for both Tier 1 and Tier 2?

Your Tier 1 preparation forms the base for Tier 2, but Tier 2 requires deeper study. For example, Quantitative Aptitude in Tier 2 has more advanced questions on Algebra, Geometry, and Trigonometry. English in Tier 2 includes essay writing and letter writing which are not in Tier 1. Start with Tier 1 level and then build up to Tier 2 difficulty.

### Is there negative marking in SSC CGL 2026?

Yes, there is negative marking in both Tier 1 and Tier 2. In Tier 1, 0.50 marks are deducted for each wrong answer. In Tier 2, the deduction varies by section — it is 1 mark for Maths and Reasoning questions and 0.25 marks for English and General Awareness questions. So be careful with guessing, especially in Tier 2.

### Are NCERT books enough for General Awareness in SSC CGL?

NCERT books from Class 6 to 10 are excellent for building your foundation in History, Geography, Polity, and Science. However, they are not enough on their own. You also need a dedicated General Knowledge book like Lucent's GK for static facts, and a current affairs source for the last 6-8 months. Combine NCERTs, Lucent's, and monthly current affairs magazines for complete coverage.

title: UPSC CSE 2026 Notification: Dates, Eligibility and How to Apply
description: UPSC Civil Services Exam 2026: complete guide covering notification dates, eligibility criteria, exam pattern for Prelims and Mains, syllabus overview.
author: Mahitosh Dey
content:
The UPSC Civil Services Examination is India's primary route into the IAS, IPS, IFS, and 24 other central services.

## What is UPSC CSE?

The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) conducts the Civil Services Examination (CSE) once a year. The process takes 12 to 14 months and has three stages: Preliminary exam, Mains exam, and Personality Test (Interview).

11 to 13 lakh candidates register each year, per UPSC Annual Reports. Roughly 800 to 1,100 make the final list across all services. Selection rate: under 0.1%.

## UPSC CSE 2026 key dates

UPSC follows a consistent annual calendar. Exact dates are published in the official Annual Calendar at upsc.gov.in. Based on the established pattern:

| Event | Expected Date |
|---|---|
| Official Notification | February 2026 |
| Application Window Opens | February 2026 |
| Last Date to Apply | March 2026 |
| Prelims Admit Card | 2 to 3 weeks before exam |
| Prelims Exam | May/June 2026 |
| Prelims Result | July to August 2026 |
| Mains Application | Within 2 weeks of Prelims result |
| Mains Exam | September 2026 |
| Mains Result | January 2027 |
| Interview / PT | February to May 2027 |
| Final Result | May to June 2027 |

> Always verify from the official source: https://upsc.gov.in. UPSC publishes the Annual Calendar in advance.

## Eligibility criteria

UPSC CSE eligibility has three main conditions: nationality, educational qualification, and age limit.

### Nationality

Must be a citizen of India for IAS and IPS. Subjects of Nepal or Bhutan, or persons of Indian origin who migrated from specific countries, are eligible for other services.

### Educational qualification

A bachelor's degree from a recognised university in any stream. Students in the final year of graduation can appear in Prelims, but the degree must be complete before Mains. UGC-recognised distance and open university degrees are also valid.

### Age limit (as on 1st August 2026)

| Category | Minimum Age | Maximum Age | Attempts Allowed |
|---|---|---|---|
| General | 21 years | 32 years | 6 |
| OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) | 21 years | 35 years | 9 |
| SC / ST | 21 years | 37 years | Unlimited (up to age limit) |
| PwBD (General) | 21 years | 42 years | 9 |
| PwBD (OBC) | 21 years | 45 years | 9 |
| PwBD (SC/ST) | 21 years | 47 years | Unlimited |

A Prelims appearance counts as one attempt, even if you don't qualify.

### Physical standards

Candidates must meet the medical standards prescribed by the Government of India. Standards vary by service. IPS and IFS have stricter physical requirements than most other services.

## Exam pattern

UPSC CSE has three stages. Each stage eliminates candidates.

### Stage 1: Preliminary exam

| Paper | Marks | Duration | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| GS Paper 1: General Studies | 200 | 2 hours | Qualifying + Screening |
| GS Paper 2: CSAT | 200 | 2 hours | Qualifying only (33% cutoff) |

Both papers are MCQ with negative marking (1/3 mark per wrong answer). CSAT is qualifying. You need just 33% (66 marks out of 200) to clear it. Your Prelims rank comes only from GS Paper 1.

GS Paper 1 covers: Current Events, Indian History, Indian Polity, Indian Economy, Geography, Environment and Ecology, and General Science.

### Stage 2: Mains exam

Mains has 9 papers. Two are qualifying; seven count for merit.

| Paper | Subject | Marks | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper A | Indian Language (from 8th Schedule) | 300 | Qualifying |
| Paper B | English | 300 | Qualifying |
| Paper I | Essay | 250 | Merit |
| Paper II | GS 1: History, Geography, Society | 250 | Merit |
| Paper III | GS 2: Governance, Constitution, IR | 250 | Merit |
| Paper IV | GS 3: Economy, Environment, Science and Tech | 250 | Merit |
| Paper V | GS 4: Ethics, Integrity, Aptitude | 250 | Merit |
| Paper VI | Optional Subject, Paper 1 | 250 | Merit |
| Paper VII | Optional Subject, Paper 2 | 250 | Merit |
| Total (merit papers) | | 1,750 | |

### Stage 3: Personality test and interview

Marks: 275. Conducted by a UPSC Board at Dholpur House, New Delhi. The board assesses personality, communication, awareness, and decision-making capacity. It's not a test of bookish knowledge.

Grand total = 1,750 (Mains) + 275 (Interview) = 2,025 marks.

## Popular optional subjects

Your optional subject covers 500 of the 1,750 Mains marks. Pick one you're genuinely interested in. You'll be reading it for 6 to 12 months.

| Optional Subject | Success Rate | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Public Administration | High | Short syllabus; overlaps with GS |
| Sociology | High | Straightforward scoring |
| History | Moderate to High | Good for humanities backgrounds |
| Geography | High | Overlaps with GS 1 |
| Anthropology | High | Short syllabus, reliable scores |
| Political Science and International Relations | Moderate to High | Good for PS graduates; overlaps with GS 2 |
| Hindi Literature | High | Strong for Hindi medium students |
| Mathematics | Moderate | Best for engineers with a strong base |

## Services you can get

Clearing CSE qualifies you for allocation to one of the following services, based on rank and preference.

#### Group A services (central)

- IAS (Indian Administrative Service)
- IPS (Indian Police Service)
- IFS (Indian Foreign Service)
- IRS (Income Tax)
- IRS (Customs and Central Excise)
- IRAS (Railway Accounts)
- IRTS (Railway Traffic Service)
- IRSME, IRSEE (Railway Engineering)
- IDAS (Defence Accounts)
- ICAS (Civil Accounts)
- IPoS (India Post)
- Plus 15 or more additional services

#### Salary (IAS example, as per 7th Pay Commission and current DA rates)

- Probationer: Rs 56,100/month + allowances
- After training: Rs 78,800 + HRA + DA + other allowances
- Senior IAS (Secretary level): Rs 2,25,000+

## How to apply online for UPSC CSE 2026

Applications are submitted online at upsconline.nic.in in two parts.

1. Go to: https://upsconline.nic.in
2. Click "Online Application for Various Examinations of UPSC"
3. Select: Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination 2026
4. Part 1 Registration: Enter basic details (name, date of birth, address, email, mobile number)
5. Part 2 Registration: Fill academic details, choose your optional subject, upload photo and signature
6. Pay Fee: Rs 100 via Net Banking, UPI, or Debit/Credit Card. SC/ST/Female/PwBD candidates are exempted from the fee.
7. Submit and print the confirmation page.

> Apply early. UPSC servers get overloaded in the last 2 to 3 days before the deadline.

## UPSC CSE preparation strategy

Preparation splits into two phases: an initial foundation phase (12 or more months out) and an exam-focused revision phase (3 to 4 months out).

### For beginners (12+ months away)

#### Step 1: Know the syllabus

Download the official UPSC CSE syllabus from upsc.gov.in. Read it fully before picking up any book.

#### Step 2: NCERT first

Start with NCERT textbooks (Class 6 to 12) for History, Geography, Polity, and Economics. These build the conceptual base for GS.

#### Step 3: Standard books for each GS paper

| Subject | Recommended Book |
|---|---|
| Indian Polity | M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity |
| Indian History | Bipin Chandra, Modern India; Old NCERT (Ancient/Medieval) |
| Geography | G.C. Leong, Certificate Physical and Human Geography |
| Indian Economy | Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy |
| Environment and Ecology | Shankar IAS, Environment |
| Ethics (GS 4) | Lexicon for Ethics, Chronicle |
| Current Affairs | The Hindu or Indian Express + a monthly magazine |

#### Step 4: Current affairs daily

Read a quality newspaper every day. The Hindu is what most candidates use. Make short notes on topics of national importance.

#### Step 5: Answer writing practice

Mains is a writing exam. Start writing 2 to 3 answers per day from month 3 or 4. Join a test series 6 months before Mains.

#### Step 6: Revise regularly

Revise your notes every 3 weeks. Forgetting is a bigger problem than not knowing. Space out your revision sessions.

### For Prelims (3 to 4 months away)

- Solve 30 UPSC previous year Prelims questions every day
- Attempt 5 to 6 full mock tests per week
- Focus on Environment, Science and Tech, and Current Affairs. These tend to shift the cutoff.
- Don't start new books. Revise your existing notes only.

## How many attempts does it take?

Most toppers clear UPSC in 3 to 5 attempts. The average is around 3. A realistic preparation timeline is 18 to 24 months; six months of intense study is rarely enough.

## Frequently asked questions

These are the questions that come up in almost every discussion about UPSC CSE eligibility and process.

#### Is a final year student eligible for UPSC CSE?

Yes. Final year students can appear in Prelims. The degree must be complete before Mains.

#### How many attempts does a General category candidate get?

6 attempts, up to the age of 32 years.

#### What is the application fee for UPSC CSE 2026?

Rs 100 for General and OBC candidates. SC/ST/Female/PwBD candidates are exempted.

#### Does a Prelims appearance count as an attempt even if I don't qualify?

Yes. A Prelims appearance counts as one attempt, even if you don't qualify for Mains.

## Final thought

UPSC CSE demands sustained effort across a broad range of subjects over 12 to 14 months per cycle. The exam tests knowledge, temperament, and clarity under pressure. Most successful candidates spent 2 to 3 years preparing before clearing. The pattern repeats across toppers: broad foundation first, answer writing practice from year 2, and at least one Prelims attempt before a serious Mains run.

## Sources

- UPSC official website: https://upsc.gov.in
- Online application portal: https://upsconline.nic.in
- UPSC Annual Reports (candidate registration and selection data)

title: IBPS PO 2026 preparation guide: Prelims, Mains, and interview
description: IBPS PO selects through three stages: Prelims, Mains, and an interview. Each stage tests different things and needs a different approach. This guide covers.
author: SarkariDarapan Team
content:
## How IBPS PO selects candidates

IBPS PO fills Probationary Officer vacancies across 11 public sector banks through a three-stage process: Prelims, Mains, and an interview. Each stage serves a different purpose.

Prelims is a qualifying filter. Mains produces the merit score. The interview contributes 20% of the final merit, with Mains carrying the remaining 80%, per IBPS's official selection process on ibps.in.

Getting this sequence wrong is the most common preparation mistake. Candidates who study Mains-level content before clearing Prelims waste weeks. Candidates who study only Prelims content and then scramble for Mains lose even more.

---

## Prelims exam structure

Prelims has 100 questions across three sections, each with its own time limit.

| Section | Questions | Marks | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| English Language | 30 | 30 | 20 minutes |
| Quantitative Aptitude | 35 | 35 | 20 minutes |
| Reasoning Ability | 35 | 35 | 20 minutes |
| Total | 100 | 100 | 60 minutes |

Negative marking is 0.25 marks per wrong answer. The sectional time limit is what catches most candidates off guard: you can't skip a weak section and return to it later. If Quantitative Aptitude is your weakest section, you still have exactly 20 minutes to clear the sectional cutoff in it.

IBPS sets both overall and sectional cutoffs for Prelims. Failing the sectional cutoff in any one section eliminates you regardless of your total score.

---

## Mains exam structure

Mains has an objective section (155 questions, 200 marks) and a descriptive paper.

| Section | Questions | Marks | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reasoning and Computer Aptitude | 45 | 60 | 60 minutes |
| Data Analysis and Interpretation | 35 | 60 | 45 minutes |
| General Economy and Banking Awareness | 40 | 40 | 35 minutes |
| English Language | 35 | 40 | 40 minutes |
| Descriptive: Letter and Essay | 2 | 25 | 30 minutes |

Negative marking in the objective section is 0.25 marks per wrong answer. The Descriptive paper runs after the objective section and is evaluated only for candidates who clear the objective cutoff.

The final merit is calculated as 80% Mains score (objective plus Descriptive) and 20% interview score, per ibps.in. Prelims marks are not counted.

---

## What changes between Prelims and Mains

Prelims and Mains test the same broad subjects but at different depths and under different constraints.

| Prelims approach | Mains approach |
|---|---|
| Clear sectional and overall cutoff | Every mark shapes final merit and rank |
| English: grammar, vocabulary, basic comprehension | English: longer passages, cloze tests, Descriptive writing |
| Quantitative Aptitude: arithmetic focus | Data Analysis and Interpretation: DI sets, caselet DI |
| Reasoning: basic puzzles, coding-decoding, syllogism | Reasoning and Computer Aptitude: multi-variable complex puzzles |
| No Banking Awareness | General Economy and Banking Awareness: 40 questions |
| No Descriptive paper | Formal letter plus essay in 30 minutes |
| 1 mock per week sufficient | 3 to 4 mocks per week, plus daily Descriptive practice |

---

## Reasoning: where Mains separates candidates

Reasoning in Prelims covers coding-decoding, blood relations, direction sense, syllogism, and basic seating arrangements. Most candidates handle this section adequately with 4 to 5 weeks of focused practice.

Mains Reasoning is a different level. Puzzles are multi-variable: a single question set might ask you to arrange 8 people across two floors with constraints on their professions, ages, and directions simultaneously. These sets take 7 to 10 minutes each. With 45 questions in 60 minutes, you can't attempt everything.

The practical approach: scan the Mains Reasoning section before starting. Spend 2 minutes identifying which sets look solvable, tackle those first, and leave the hardest sets for last. Candidates who score well in Mains Reasoning typically attempt 30 to 35 of the 45 questions and score around 38 to 45 marks, not by rushing through everything.

---

## Quantitative Aptitude vs Data Analysis and Interpretation

Prelims Quant is arithmetic-heavy: percentages, profit and loss, time and work, ratios, averages, number series. These topics are solvable with formula knowledge and timed practice.

Mains replaces Quant with Data Analysis and Interpretation. DI sets dominate: bar graphs, pie charts, line graphs, and caselet DI (paragraph-based data that requires reading and extracting numbers before calculating). A single DI set can have 5 questions requiring 4 to 5 separate calculations each.

The difficulty jump is real if you haven't practiced DI. The fix is simple: from the third week of Mains preparation onward, solve two DI sets per day. Include caselet DI specifically, since those appear in every IBPS PO Mains cycle and take the most time per mark earned.

---

## Banking Awareness: the section that trips unprepared candidates

Banking Awareness carries 40 questions and 40 marks in Mains, with no equivalent in Prelims. It's the section most candidates underestimate.

The syllabus splits into two parts. Static Banking Awareness covers: Reserve Bank of India's structure and functions, monetary policy tools (repo rate, reverse repo rate, CRR, SLR), types of bank accounts, NEFT and RTGS and IMPS basics, priority sector lending norms, NPA classifications, and banking regulators. Dynamic Banking Awareness covers: RBI policy announcements from the last 6 months, major bank mergers, government financial schemes, and Union Budget highlights relevant to banking.

Start static Banking Awareness in Month 1, not Month 3. It takes longer to retain than current affairs because the concepts are unfamiliar to candidates without a banking or finance background. Two weeks of Banking Awareness prep before Mains is not enough to retain the static portion. Three months of 30 minutes daily is.

---

## The Descriptive paper: 25 marks most candidates leave behind

The Descriptive paper in IBPS PO Mains asks candidates to write one formal letter (150 to 200 words) and one essay (200 to 250 words) in 30 minutes. Most candidates prepare for it last, or skip it entirely, and leave 10 to 15 marks on the table.

What the Descriptive paper tests: formal writing structure, appropriate vocabulary, and the ability to develop an argument within a word limit. Topics in past IBPS PO Mains cycles have included "Role of technology in the banking sector," "Financial inclusion in rural India," and "Benefits of digital payments." These topics repeat in format even when the exact subject changes.

The preparation approach: learn 8 to 10 formal letter formats (complaint, request, feedback, editor letters). For essays, practice writing 200 words on a topic in 10 minutes, twice per week. After 3 weeks of this routine, the pace becomes manageable. There are no shortcuts here, only repetition.

---

## The interview: 20% of your final score

20% of the final IBPS PO merit comes from the interview stage, per ibps.in. Most candidates treat interview preparation as an afterthought after Mains. For anyone whose Mains score puts them near the cutoff, that 20% is not optional.

Interview panels typically ask: current RBI repo rate and recent monetary policy decisions, why you want to join banking (specific reasons, not generic ones), about the specific bank you're interviewing at (its recent performance, CEO, headquarters, tagline), and standard questions about your education and background.

The prep is targeted. Read the specific bank's most recent annual report highlights and press releases. Know the current RBI Governor and the repo rate as of the interview date. Prepare a structured 90-second "tell me about yourself" that includes a genuine reason for choosing banking. Two weeks of focused preparation is enough.

---

## A practical preparation sequence

IBPS PO preparation works best in three phases aligned to the exam stages.

In Month 1, focus on Prelims fundamentals across all three sections: one full mock per week and 30 minutes of static Banking Awareness daily. Don't wait to start Banking Awareness. It's tempting to save it for later, but the retention curve doesn't work that way.

In Month 2, shift Prelims practice to mock-test pace while introducing DI sets and complex Reasoning puzzles as a warm-up for Mains. Take two Prelims mocks per week. Banking Awareness continues daily.

After Prelims results are out, switch entirely to Mains: three to four full Mains mocks per week, daily Descriptive writing practice, and dynamic Banking Awareness (last 6 months). Start two weeks of interview preparation in the final stretch before the Mains date.

Starting Banking Awareness in Month 1 instead of Month 3 is one of the few things that makes a measurable difference in how Mains goes.

---

## Frequently asked questions

**Is IBPS PO harder than SSC CGL?**
They test different things. IBPS PO has Banking Awareness and a Descriptive paper that SSC CGL doesn't. SSC CGL Mains has a broader subject spread. IBPS PO also adds an interview stage worth 20% of the final score. Candidates from non-banking backgrounds typically find Banking Awareness the hardest adjustment when switching from SSC preparation to IBPS PO.

**What is the final merit formula for IBPS PO?**
The final merit is 80% of the Mains score (objective plus Descriptive) and 20% of the interview score, per IBPS's official CRP PO notification on ibps.in. Prelims marks are not counted in the final selection.

**When does the IBPS PO 2026 notification come out?**
IBPS PO notifications typically release in August, with Prelims in October and Mains in November. Check ibps.in for the official 2026 calendar once it is published.

**What is the age limit for IBPS PO?**
General and EWS candidates must be between 20 and 30 years of age. OBC candidates get a 3-year relaxation (up to 33 years). SC and ST candidates get a 5-year relaxation (up to 35 years), per IBPS's official eligibility criteria on ibps.in. Age is calculated as of the notification date.

**Is Banking Awareness tested in Prelims?**
No. Banking Awareness and General Economy appear only in the Mains examination under the "General Economy and Banking Awareness" section (40 questions, 40 marks). Prelims tests only English Language, Quantitative Aptitude, and Reasoning Ability.

**How long does IBPS PO preparation take from scratch?**
6 months is a reasonable timeline for most candidates starting from zero, at 4 to 5 hours of daily study. Candidates with prior SSC or similar exam preparation often clear Prelims faster but still need the full 6 months to be competitive in Mains, mainly because of Banking Awareness and the Descriptive paper.

title: SSC CGL Tier 1 vs Tier 2: 2026 Prep Strategy for Each
description: Most SSC CGL aspirants prep the same for both tiers. Tier 1 sets the cutoff. Tier 2 sets your rank. Here is how to adjust preparation after clearing Tier 1.
author: SarkariDarapan Team
content:
## Tier 1 and Tier 2 are not the same exam

Tier 1 is a qualifying filter. Whether you score 162 or 185 doesn't matter as long as you're above the cutoff. The General category Tier 1 cutoff for SSC CGL 2023 was approximately 160 marks out of 200, per SSC's official result published on ssc.gov.in. Getting past that number is the only goal at this stage.

Tier 2 is different. Every mark you score goes directly toward your final rank and determines which post you're allocated. An Inspector in CBIC and a Tax Assistant in Income Tax can both clear Tier 1 with 163 marks. What separates them is Tier 2 performance.

That distinction changes how you should prepare for each stage.

---

## Tier 1 exam structure

Tier 1 has 100 questions across four sections, answered in 60 minutes.

| Section | Questions | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| General Intelligence and Reasoning | 25 | 50 |
| General Awareness | 25 | 50 |
| Quantitative Aptitude | 25 | 50 |
| English Comprehension | 25 | 50 |
| Total | 100 | 200 |

Negative marking is 0.5 marks per wrong answer. 60 minutes for 100 questions is 36 seconds per question. At that pace, you can't work things out from scratch. Speed comes from pattern recognition built through repeated practice.

---

## Tier 2 exam structure

The Tier 2 structure changed significantly in 2022. Paper 1 is now compulsory for all candidates, with three sections in a module-based format.

| Module | Subject | Questions | Marks each |
|---|---|---|---|
| Section 1, Module 1 | Mathematical Abilities | 30 | 3 |
| Section 1, Module 1 | Reasoning and General Intelligence | 30 | 3 |
| Section 1, Module 2 | English Language and Comprehension | 45 | 3 |
| Section 1, Module 2 | General Awareness | 25 | 3 |
| Section 2, Module 1 | Computer Knowledge | 20 | 3 |

Paper 1 total: 450 marks. Negative marking is 1 mark per wrong answer, up from 0.5 in Tier 1.

Candidates who applied for Junior Statistical Officer (JSO) sit an additional Paper 2 (Statistics, 200 marks). Candidates who applied for Assistant Audit Officer (AAO) sit Paper 3 (General Studies: Finance and Economics, 200 marks). Both are restricted to candidates who opted for these posts during the initial application.

---

## What changes in Tier 2 Maths

In Tier 1, the 25 Maths questions are heavily arithmetic-weighted: percentages, profit and loss, time and work, simple and compound interest. Candidates who are solid on arithmetic can clear the Tier 1 cutoff without much work in geometry or trigonometry.
